front_matter.purpose:
# Purpose of This Manual

This Policy & Procedure Manual sets out how **[AGENCY NAME]** operates its Assisted Living Facility (ALF) in the State of Texas. The facility is licensed as a **[Type A / Type B]** ALF by the Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC), Long-term Care Regulation (LTCR), under Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 247 and 26 TAC Chapter 553. Where **[AGENCY NAME]** participates in Medicaid through STAR+PLUS Home and Community Based Services (HCBS) assisted living, the manual also covers the program requirements that apply to that participation.

The manual is intended to:

- Turn the licensing rules into clear, written, day-to-day procedures that staff can follow.
- Protect the health, safety, dignity, and rights of every resident, including freedom from abuse, neglect, exploitation, and improper restraint.
- Give managers, attendants, nurses, medication aides, and support staff one consistent reference for staffing, training, hiring, admission, care coordination, resident rights, records, postings, reporting, and emergency preparedness.
- Show HHSC surveyors, managed care organizations (MCOs), the ombudsman program, residents, and families that **[AGENCY NAME]** has written policies and follows them.

This manual is an operational tool. It does not replace the statutes and rules it refers to, and it is not legal advice. If anything here conflicts with the current text of a statute, rule, or HHSC guidance, **the current law controls**. Consult the rule text, HHSC LTCR, or qualified counsel when in doubt.

# How to Use This Manual

## 1. Customize it before use
This manual is a **template**. It is not ready to use until **[AGENCY NAME]** has tailored it to the facility. Before adoption:

- Replace every **[AGENCY NAME]** placeholder and every other bracketed field (facility name, license number, license type, licensed capacity, manager and backup manager, Emergency Preparedness Coordinator and alternate, contact numbers, and so on).
- Select the options that match your license: **Type A or Type B**; **small (16 or fewer residents) or large (17 or more)**; whether you hold **Alzheimer's certification** (Type B only); whether you market **memory care**; and whether you contract with **STAR+PLUS MCOs**.
- Delete or mark 'not applicable' any section that does not apply to your facility, and add facility-specific procedures where the template is general.
- Fill in every facility-specific policy the rules require (for example, staffing ratios based on residents' service plans, the normal 24-hour staffing pattern, and the advance directive, vaccine, and infection-control policies).

## 2. Items to confirm against the rule text
Some rule text was not fully retrieved when this manual was prepared. Read the following in full before finalizing the related policies:

- **26 TAC §553.255** (all-staff policy for residents with Alzheimer's disease or a related disorder): confirm the required policy content.
- **26 TAC §553.261(g)** (restraints and seclusion): the subsection text was cut off in the copy reviewed.
- **26 TAC §553.272** (advertisements, solicitations, and promotional material): draft the policy after reading the rule, and note §553.259(a)(4) on memory care marketing.
- **26 TAC §553.275** (emergency preparedness): review the subsections after (i)(2)(D)(i), including staff accompaniment, training, drills, and return.
- **26 TAC Subchapter G** (inspections, investigations, and informal dispute resolution) and **Subchapter H** (enforcement): the sections were identified but the text was not reviewed.

## 3. Adopt it formally
The manual takes effect only after the facility's **governing body** (owner, board, or other governing authority of **[AGENCY NAME]**) formally adopts it. Record the adoption date, the approving individual or body, and the version number on the adoption page. Keep the signed adoption record with the manual.

## 4. Keep it current
- Review the whole manual **at least annually**, and sooner whenever a statute, rule, HHSC provider letter, STAR+PLUS Handbook provision, or MCO contract term changes.
- Review and update the emergency plan on the schedule 26 TAC §553.275 requires: annually, and within 30 days after an event, a drill shortcoming, or a rule change.
- Date every revision, record what changed, have the governing body approve it, and remove superseded copies from circulation.
- Give residents and representatives written notice of changes to resident policies before they take effect, as 26 TAC §553.259(c) requires.

## 5. Train all staff on it
Staff must be **trained on this manual**, not merely given a copy.

- Cover the manual in new-employee orientation, and document the training in the personnel file.
- Retrain staff when policies change and as part of the annual in-service and continuing education the rules require.
- Keep the manual where every shift can reach it, and keep sign-in sheets, competency evaluations, and certificates according to your records retention policy.
- Managers should check regularly that day-to-day practice matches the written policy.

## 6. Reading the citations
Each policy section cites the rule or guidance it implements, using the exact cite text (for example, 26 TAC §553.273). Use the citations to go to the source. Items marked 'review' call for a direct read of the rule before you rely on the template language.

# Regulatory Framework

The facility operates under the authorities below. Cites are given exactly as they appear in the source list. Regulator contact information follows.

## A. Licensing statute and general rules
- **Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 247**: Assisted Living Facility Licensing Act (statutory basis for ALF licensure by HHSC, including plan review under §247.0261 per HHSC guidance).
- **26 TAC §553.3**: Definitions (small facility: 16 or fewer residents; large facility: 17 or more).
- **26 TAC §553.5**: Types of Assisted Living Facilities (Type A and Type B).
- **26 TAC §§553.17, 553.19, 553.21, 553.23**: Licensing criteria, general application requirements, time periods, and initial license procedures.
- **26 TAC §553.27; §§553.33, 553.39**: Alzheimer's certification of a Type B facility or unit; license renewal; capacity change.
- **26 TAC §553.47**: License Fees.
- **26 TAC Subchapter D (§§553.100–553.249), incl. §553.215 and §553.225**: Facility construction and fire protection systems for new small Type A and Type B facilities.
- **26 TAC Subchapter F (§§553.301–553.311)**: Additional licensing standards for certified Alzheimer's assisted living facilities.

## B. Operating standards (Chapter 553, Subchapter E)
- **26 TAC §553.253**: Employee Qualifications and Training.
- **26 TAC §553.254**: Training Requirements for Staff Providing Personal Care Services to a Resident With Alzheimer's Disease or a Related Disorder in a Facility that is Not an Alzheimer's Certified Facility.
- **26 TAC §553.255**: All Staff Policy for Residents with Alzheimer's Disease or a Related Disorder (*confirm required content against the rule text*).
- **26 TAC §553.257**: Human Resources.
- **26 TAC §553.259**: Admission Policies and Procedures.
- **26 TAC §553.261**: Coordination of Care (*review subsection (g), restraints and seclusion, in the full rule*).
- **26 TAC §553.263**: Health maintenance activities.
- **26 TAC §553.265**: Resident Records and Retention.
- **26 TAC §553.267**: Rights.
- **26 TAC §553.269**: Access to Residents and Records by the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program.
- **26 TAC §553.271**: Postings.
- **26 TAC §553.272**: Advertisements, Solicitations, and Promotional Material (*text not reviewed; read the rule before drafting*).
- **26 TAC §553.273**: Abuse, Neglect, or Exploitation Reportable to HHSC by Facilities.
- **26 TAC §553.275**: Emergency Preparedness and Response (*review the subsections not yet retrieved*).

## C. Inspections and enforcement
- **26 TAC Subchapter G (§§553.327–553.337)**: Inspections, investigations, and informal dispute resolution (*text not reviewed*).
- **26 TAC Subchapter H (Divisions 1–10)**: Enforcement, including administrative penalties, license actions, and plans of correction (*text not reviewed*).

## D. Employment screening
- **Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 250 (incl. §250.003, §250.006)**: Nurse Aide Registry and criminal history checks for facility employees. §250.006 lists the convictions that bar employment and is referenced in 26 TAC §553.257.

## E. Medicaid / STAR+PLUS HCBS assisted living
- **1 TAC §353.1153**: STAR+PLUS Home and Community Based Services (HCBS) Program.
- **STAR+PLUS Handbook §7200 (Assisted Living Services), incl. §§7211, 7221, 7240–7241.1, 7250–7252**.
- **42 CFR §438.602**: State responsibilities, including screening and enrollment of managed care network providers.

## F. Guidance and related law
- **HHSC Provider Letter (PL) 2023-22**: Medication services in assisted living facilities.
- **42 USC §3058g(b); 45 CFR §1324.11(e)(2)**: Federal basis for ombudsman access to facilities, residents, and records, as incorporated in 26 TAC §553.269(b)–(c).
- **Texas Human Resources Code Chapter 123 (§§123.004, 123.006, 123.008)**: Community Homes for Disabled Persons Location Act (applies where an ALF licensed under HSC Chapter 247 qualifies as a community home).

> Rules change. Verify each citation against the current official text before relying on it, and use the 'Keep it current' process in *How to Use This Manual*.

citations.title: Employee Qualifications and Training
citations.requirement: (a) The facility designates a manager in writing. The manager must be on duty 40 hrs/week and may manage only one facility, except a small Type A manager may oversee up to 4 facilities with no more than 16 residents in total. A backup is named in writing. Large-facility managers need an associate's degree, a bachelor's degree, or a high school credential plus 1 year of management experience. The manager completes a 24-hr ALF management course by the first anniversary, including 8 hrs on the standards within 3 months, plus 12 hrs of CE a year. (b) An attendant is in the facility whenever residents are present. (c) Staffing policies set ratios from residents' service plans. The normal 24-hr staffing pattern is disclosed before admission and posted monthly. Night staff: small Type A immediately available; large Type A and all Type B immediately available and awake. (d) 4-hr orientation for all staff. 16 hrs of attendant on-the-job training in the first 16 hrs after orientation. 6 hrs/yr of direct-care education, including 1 hr fall prevention and 1 hr behavior management. Annual geriatric in-service for nurses, CNAs and medication aides.

citations.title: Training Requirements for Staff Providing Personal Care Services to a Resident With Alzheimer's Disease or a Related Disorder in a Facility that is Not an Alzheimer's Certified Facility
citations.requirement: Manager: 4 hrs of training plus a competency evaluation, then 2 hrs of annual CE. Personal care staff: 4 hrs plus a competency evaluation before performing personal care, then 2 hrs of CE. Non-direct staff with recurring contact (housekeeping, front desk, maintenance) complete training and a competency evaluation on Alzheimer's disease, person-centered care and behaviors. Certificates are issued to staff and kept per records retention policy. Training carries over if the employment gap is under 2 years.

citations.title: All Staff Policy for Residents with Alzheimer's Disease or a Related Disorder
citations.requirement: Requires a facility policy on all staff and residents with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders. Section number and title verified from the Subchapter E table of contents, and §553.254(a)(2) confirms the §553.254 training may satisfy it. The full text was not retrieved, so confirm the policy's required content against the rule before finalizing.

citations.title: Human Resources
citations.requirement: Personnel files hold: criminal history check documentation; annual Employee Misconduct Registry (EMR) and Nurse Aide Registry (NAR) checks; TB screening; vaccine-policy compliance or exemption; the signed statement on criminal liability for failure to report; and a signed disclosure statement on §250.006 convictions and residence in another state in the past 5 years. Before hire, search the EMR and NAR. Do not hire or keep anyone listed as unemployable or convicted of a barring offense. Repeat searches at least every 12 months. A name-based criminal check is required in each prior state of residence in the past 5 years; the person may be hired pending results but not in a direct-contact position. Suspend, and do not reinstate, an employee HHSC finds engaged in reportable conduct until appeals are exhausted. Reportable conduct includes abuse or neglect causing harm, sexual abuse, financial exploitation of $25 or more, and emotional or verbal abuse causing harm.

citations.title: Admission Policies and Procedures
citations.requirement: (a) Do not admit or retain a resident whose needs cannot be met. Use a written admission agreement. Give the disclosure statement and rate schedule. Provide the Memory Care Disclosure Statement if memory care is marketed (plus HHSC Form 3641 if Alzheimer's certified). Physician exam within 30 days before or 14 days after admission. Collect the listed identifying information. (b) Comprehensive assessment and service plan within 14 days of admission. Update the plan annually and on significant change. (c) Give the disclosure statement before admission and the Resident's Bill of Rights. Give and document family receipt of the HHSC abuse hotline number. Keep written resident policies and give notice of changes before they take effect. Give the restraint/seclusion notice and the emergency plan or evacuation summary. (d) Advance directive policy and notice. $500 penalty for failure to inform. (e) Inappropriate placement: Forms 1124, 1125, 1126 within 10 working days; evacuation waiver; discharge within 30 days if the facility will not retain.

citations.title: Coordination of Care
citations.requirement: (a) Medication administration, supervision, self-administration, storage and disposal. (b) Accident, injury and acute illness response and documentation; first aid supplies. (c) Health care professionals and outside HCSSA services; no ongoing nursing-facility-level services. (d) Activity program at least weekly. (e) Dietary services. (f) Infection prevention and control, TB screening and the vaccine policy. (g) Restraints and seclusion (the heading was verified, but the subsection text was cut off in the retrieved copy; review it before finalizing).

citations.title: Health maintenance activities
citations.requirement: Personal care staff may perform a health maintenance activity (HMA) without delegation only when an RN has assessed and documented that it qualifies. The resident or representative must direct the task and agree in writing, and the condition must be stable and predictable. The RN reassesses on any change of condition, at least annually, and at least every 6 months for residents with Alzheimer's or in a certified facility or unit. Activities that are not HMAs require RN delegation under 22 TAC Chapter 225 and §553.261(a)(1)(A)(iii).

citations.title: Resident Records and Retention
citations.requirement: Records are confidential and safeguarded. A record contains the admission form, assessments, service plan, physician orders, advance directives, the physician exam, professional service documentation, and guardianship papers. Records are available to residents, legal representatives and HHSC. Keep a simple financial record of charges and of any personal funds handled. Issue receipts on request. Request the guardianship court order and letters at admission and at each annual assessment, make a follow-up request within 30 days, and keep the results.

citations.title: Rights
citations.requirement: (a) Give each resident the Residents' Bill of Rights and post it in each resident's primary language. The rights include freedom from abuse and from restraint used for discipline or convenience, restraint only on written physician authorization or in an emergency, and complaint without reprisal. They also include unopened mail, visitors at any reasonable hour, managing one's own finances with at least quarterly accounting, record access, choice of physician, participation in the service plan, refusal of treatment, a locked personal area, notice by day 30 of Medicare/Medicaid entitlement, discharge only on listed grounds with 30 days' written notice, and ombudsman access. (b) Post the Providers' Bill of Rights. A provider may terminate for just cause on 30 days' written notice, or immediately for a serious threat after notice to HHSC at 1-800-458-9858. (c) Allow HHSC access. (d) Authorized electronic monitoring (AEM).

citations.title: Access to Residents and Records by the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program
citations.requirement: The State Ombudsman, certified ombudsmen and interns get immediate, private, unimpeded access to the facility and to residents during business or visiting hours. The State Ombudsman and certified ombudsmen also get access at other times if circumstances require. They get access to resident records with consent or as the rule otherwise allows. HIPAA does not bar release to the ombudsman, who is a health oversight agency.

citations.title: Postings
citations.requirement: Post in a public area: the license; the HHSC complaint-procedure sign; the notice that inspection reports are available and the HHSC toll-free number; the most recent inspection report; the Residents' Bill of Rights; the Providers' Bill of Rights; the local ombudsman number and the 1-800-252-2412 toll-free number; the normal 24-hr staffing pattern; and the sign 'Cases of Suspected Abuse, Neglect, or Exploitation must be reported to HHSC by calling 1-800-458-9858.'

citations.title: Advertisements, Solicitations, and Promotional Material
citations.requirement: Rules on advertising and promotional material. Section number and title verified from the Subchapter E table of contents. The text was not retrieved, so draft the policy after reading the rule. Note §553.259(a)(4) on memory care marketing.

citations.title: Abuse, Neglect, or Exploitation Reportable to HHSC by Facilities
citations.requirement: Staff with cause to believe a resident has been or may be harmed by abuse, neglect or exploitation, or died from abuse or neglect, report to HHSC at 1-800-458-9858 (or the HHSC website) and to municipal police or the county sheriff. The report includes the resident's name, age and address, the responsible person, the nature of the condition, the basis of knowledge, and other relevant information. The facility makes an immediate oral report, investigates, and sends a written investigation report to the HHSC state office no later than the 5th calendar day after the oral report. No retaliation. Staff sign a statement, as a condition of employment, that they may be criminally liable for failure to report. The facility follows its internal prevention, detection and reporting policies.

citations.title: Emergency Preparedness and Response
citations.requirement: Document a risk assessment (fire, outage, flood, hurricane or severe weather, epidemic, cyber attack, etc.). Keep a written plan covering the 8 core functions: direction and control, warning, communication, sheltering, evacuation, transportation, health and medical needs, and resource management. Coordinate with the local Emergency Management Coordinator. Designate an Emergency Preparedness Coordinator and an alternate. Review and update the plan annually and within 30 days after an event, drill shortcoming or rule change. Give residents and representatives the plan or an evacuation summary at admission. Register with 2-1-1 Texas and tell residents how to register for evacuation assistance. Shelter-in-place temperatures must be 68–82°F. Notify the HHSC regional office and the EMC on a decision to shelter or evacuate. Keep written acknowledgments with a receiving facility and an alternate. Plan for pets and service animals. Only subsections (a)–(i)(2)(D)(i) were retrieved; review the remaining subsections (staff accompaniment, training, drills, return) before finalizing.

citations.title: Types of Assisted Living Facilities
citations.requirement: Type A: residents can evacuate without staff help, with no routine night attendance. Type B: residents may need evacuation help and night attendance but may not be permanently bedfast.

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: Small facility: licensed for 16 or fewer residents. Large facility: 17 or more. Defines terms used in the staffing, HMA, infection control and AEM rules.

citations.title: Licensing criteria, general application requirements, time periods, initial license procedures
citations.requirement: Initial application through the HHSC portal (TULIP) with the local fire authority documentation and the pre-licensure training certificate. A Life Safety Code inspection and a health inspection are required. After the LSC inspection, 1–3 residents may be admitted. HHSC must deny an applicant whose health care or long-term care license was revoked within the last 5 years or who is excluded from Medicare/Medicaid (§553.17). Applications still incomplete 120 days after receipt are denied (§553.21).

citations.title: License Fees
citations.requirement: 3-year license fee of $300 + $15 per bed, capped at $2,250. Alzheimer's certification +$300. $15 per bed for a capacity increase. Late-renewal fee of half the basic fee if filed later than 45 days before expiration. Possible trust fund assessment (§553.47(d)). Expedited LSC inspection fee (§553.47(g)).

citations.title: Facility Construction; Fire Protection Systems for New Small Type A / Type B Facilities
citations.requirement: Construction and life safety standards in separate divisions for existing and new facilities, small and large, Type A and Type B. New small Type A and Type B facilities need an NFPA 13, 13R or 13D sprinkler system with electrical supervision, and a manual fire alarm with smoke detection (§§553.215, 553.225). Residents' evacuation capability must match the NFPA 101 and Subchapter D requirements (§553.259(a)(1)).

citations.title: Additional Licensing Standards for Certified Alzheimer's Assisted Living Facilities
citations.requirement: Added staffing, training, admission, disclosure (Form 3641) and physical plant standards (§553.311) for an Alzheimer's certified facility or unit. Certification applies to Type B only (§553.27).

citations.title: Inspections, Investigations, and Informal Dispute Resolution
citations.requirement: HHSC inspections and complaint investigations, and the informal dispute resolution process. Section range verified from the Chapter 553 table of contents; text not retrieved.

citations.title: Enforcement
citations.requirement: Enforcement remedies, including administrative penalties, license actions and plans of correction. Subchapter verified from the Chapter 553 table of contents; text not retrieved.

citations.title: Nurse Aide Registry and Criminal History Checks for Facility Employees
citations.requirement: Verify employability through criminal history and registry checks, with an annual registry search. §250.006 lists the convictions that bar employment (referenced in §553.257).

citations.title: Assisted Living Facility Licensing Act
citations.requirement: Statutory basis for ALF licensure by HHSC, including plan review (§247.0261, per HHSC guidance).

citations.title: STAR+PLUS Home and Community Based Services (HCBS) Program
citations.requirement: STAR+PLUS HCBS eligibility and interest-list rules for members who may receive assisted living services.

citations.title: STAR+PLUS Handbook – Assisted Living Services
citations.requirement: Housing options (apartment vs non-apartment) are stated in the MCO contract. Members live in an ALF contracted with their MCO. Health assessment and emergency training within 3 days of admission. At least 4 social activities a week. Next-business-day reporting of changes to the MCO. Member trust fund records. Room and board cannot be waived (a lower amount may be accepted), is prorated in the first month, and is due on a written date.

citations.title: Medication services in assisted living facilities
citations.requirement: HHSC guidance on medication administration, supervision and self-administration. Only a licensed nurse, a permitted medication aide under a nurse on duty or on call, or an RN-delegated employee may administer medications. A medication aide permit takes 100 classroom + 20 lab + 10 clinical hours and an exam, with annual renewal.

citations.title: State responsibilities – screening and enrollment of managed care network providers
citations.requirement: Managed care network providers, including STAR+PLUS ALFs, must be screened and enrolled with the State.

citations.title: Alzheimer's certification of a Type B facility or unit; license renewal; capacity change
citations.requirement: Only a Type B facility or unit may be Alzheimer's certified (§553.27). Renew the license on time (§553.33). Get HHSC approval before adding beds (§553.39). Sections are present in the research section list; text not re-fetched.

citations.title: Community Homes for Disabled Persons Location Act
citations.requirement: An ALF licensed under HSC Ch. 247 can qualify as a community home. Up to 6 persons with disabilities + 2 supervisors. No community home within one-half mile of another.

citations.title: Ombudsman access to facilities, residents and records
citations.requirement: Federal basis for the ombudsman's access rights, as incorporated in 26 TAC §553.269(b)–(c).

policies.title: Organization, Licensee and Manager Responsibilities
policies.applies_to: Licensee/owner, manager, backup manager, and all staff of [AGENCY NAME], a Texas Assisted Living Facility (Type A / Type B) licensed by HHSC Long-term Care Regulation
policies.purpose: To establish who is accountable for operating [AGENCY NAME] under HSC Chapter 247 and 26 TAC Chapter 553. This policy sets the manager's designation, qualifications, training, and availability, and the licensee's duty to keep the facility's license category matched to the residents it serves.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] designates a manager in writing with authority over daily operations. The manager is on duty at least 40 hours per week and manages only this facility, except where the small Type A exception below applies. A competent employee is named in writing to act when the manager is absent. The manager meets the education and training requirements for the facility's size and completes required Alzheimer's/dementia training. The licensee documents the facility's license category (Type A or Type B; small or large) and checks every resident's evacuation capability against it. Staff are paid at no less than the applicable minimum wage.

definitions.definition: A facility whose residents are capable of evacuating without staff help and that has no routine night attendance requirement.
A facility that may serve residents who need help to evacuate and who need night attendance. Residents may not be permanently bedfast.
A facility licensed for 16 or fewer residents.
A facility licensed for 17 or more residents.
The person designated in writing by the licensee who is responsible for operating the facility day to day.
An employee named in writing who is competent and authorized to act in the manager's absence.

procedures: The licensee designates the manager in a signed written designation that states the manager's authority over facility operations. The designation is filed in the administrative file and in the manager's personnel record.

Before designation, the licensee verifies qualifications. For a small facility the manager must hold a high school diploma or equivalent. For a large facility (17+ residents) the manager must hold an associate's degree (nursing, health care management or a related field), a bachelor's degree, or a high school credential plus 1 year of management experience. Copies of credentials and experience verification are kept in the personnel record.
The manager is scheduled on duty at least 40 hours per week. The manager's timesheets or schedules are kept to show the 40 hours.

The manager manages only this facility. The only exception is a small Type A manager who oversees up to 4 facilities with no more than 16 residents in total. That manager must be reachable by phone or pager while off-site, and the contact number is posted and given to staff. If this exception is used, the licensee records the facilities and the total resident count and reviews the count monthly.
The licensee names a backup manager in writing. The written designation is dated, signed by the licensee, and filed with the manager designation. It is updated whenever the backup changes.
The manager posts and shares with all staff a current list showing who is in charge on every shift, including the manager's phone number or pager and the backup manager's number.

Within 3 months of hire, the manager completes 8 hours of training on the Chapter 553 standards. By the first anniversary of hire, the manager completes the full 24-hour assisted living management course from a qualified outside provider.
The administrator checks that the training is a recognized course. Facility in-services do not count toward the 24 hours. The training file records the course content, hours, dates, and provider.

If the manager claims an exemption (a comparable prior course, or a move between licensed ALFs with a break of 30 days or less), the licensee collects proof of the prior course or of the dates of employment and keeps it in the file before the exemption is applied.

Each year the manager completes 12 hours of continuing education covering at least two of the content areas listed in the rule. Certificates are filed in the personnel record. The licensee reviews each manager's CE hours quarterly so shortfalls are corrected before year-end.

The manager completes 4 hours of Alzheimer's/dementia training and passes a competency evaluation, then completes 2 hours of continuing education annually. The same requirement applies to the backup manager when they act as manager. Certificates are issued to the manager and kept in the personnel record.

The licensee records the facility's license category (Type A or B; small or large) in the administrative file. At every pre-admission screening, assessment, reassessment, and significant change, the manager documents each resident's evacuation capability. If a resident's capability no longer fits the license category, the manager starts the process in ADM-04 and ADM-05 the same day.
The licensee reviews payroll at least annually and whenever rates change. It confirms that every employee is paid at no less than the applicable minimum wage and that overtime is paid as required.
The licensee reviews this policy annually and whenever a manager or backup manager changes. Changes are recorded under GOV-03.

responsibilities.duty: Designates the manager and backup in writing, verifies qualifications, funds required training, keeps the license category current, and ensures payroll compliance.
Is on duty 40 hours per week, runs daily operations, completes required courses on time, and tracks resident evacuation capability against the license category.
Acts with the manager's authority during absences and completes the required Alzheimer's/dementia training.
Maintain the training tracker and file certificates.

documentation: Signed manager designation and backup manager designation
Manager credentials and experience verification
Manager schedule or timesheets showing 40 hours per week
Management course certificates (8-hour standards training and 24-hour course) with content, hours, dates and provider
Annual 12-hour CE certificates
Alzheimer's/dementia 4-hour and annual 2-hour training certificates and competency evaluations
Records of any exemption claimed
Record of license category and resident evacuation capability reviews
Payroll review records

policies.title: Licensure, Renewal and Regulatory Compliance
policies.applies_to: Licensee, manager, and administrative staff of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] obtains and keeps a valid HHSC license, renews on time, pays required fees, gets approval before changes in capacity or certification, and responds correctly to inspections, investigations, and enforcement.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] operates only under a current HHSC Long-term Care Regulation license as a Type A or Type B assisted living facility. The license is issued for 3 years. The facility files applications and changes through HHSC's TULIP portal. It renews at least 45 days before expiration, pays all required fees, and does not add beds or begin Alzheimer's certification without HHSC approval. The facility cooperates with Life Safety Code and health inspections and with investigations and uses the informal dispute resolution and enforcement processes in Chapter 553.

definitions.definition: The HHSC portal through which ALF license applications and changes are filed.
An HHSC inspection of the building's fire and life safety features. It is required in addition to the health inspection.
HHSC certification available only to a Type B facility or a Type B unit.

A home for persons with disabilities that qualifies under Human Resources Code Chapter 123. An ALF licensed under HSC Chapter 247 can qualify. A community home houses up to 6 persons with disabilities plus 2 supervisors, and none may be within one-half mile of another.

procedures: Before applying for an initial license, the licensee confirms the applicant and controlling persons are not excluded from Medicare/Medicaid and have not had a health care or long-term care license revoked within the past 5 years. HHSC must deny such an applicant.

The licensee files the initial application through TULIP on HHSC Form 3720. It includes documentation from the local fire authority and the pre-licensure training certificate. Form 3721 is added if Alzheimer's certification is sought. A copy of every submission and the confirmation is kept in the licensure file.

For new construction or renovation, the licensee obtains plan review under HSC Chapter 247. The building must meet the construction and life safety standards in Subchapter D for its size and type. A new small Type A or Type B facility must have an NFPA 13, 13R or 13D sprinkler system with electrical supervision and a manual fire alarm with smoke detection.

The administrator tracks the application timeline. HHSC reviews within 30 days and issues the license within 30 days after all requirements are met. An application still incomplete 120 days after receipt is denied, so the administrator answers every HHSC request promptly and records the date of each response.

The facility passes the Life Safety Code inspection and the health inspection before it is licensed. After the LSC inspection, 1 to 3 residents may be admitted as the rule allows. The facility does not admit more residents until HHSC allows it.
Only a Type B facility or unit may seek Alzheimer's certification. The licensee files Form 3721 and pays the $300 certification fee.
The licensee pays the 3-year license fee of $300 plus $15 per bed, capped at $2,250. Payment confirmations are filed.

The administrator calendars the renewal deadline and files the renewal at least 45 days before the license expires. A later filing adds a late fee of half the basic fee. The calendar alert is set at 120 days and 60 days before expiration.
Before adding beds, the licensee obtains HHSC approval, pays $15 per added bed, and confirms the building meets the construction rules for the new capacity. No added bed is occupied before approval.
If HHSC assesses a trust fund fee, the administrator pays it within 90 days of the notice and files the proof of payment.

The license is posted as required in GOV-06. The administrator keeps the HHSC contacts available to managers: Licensing 512-438-2630, LTC_ALF_ICF_Licensing@hhs.texas.gov; LTCR Policy 512-438-3161, LTCRPolicy@hhs.texas.gov; complaint and incident intake 800-458-9858.

If the facility relies on community-home status (6 or fewer residents), the licensee keeps zoning documentation and documentation of the half-mile spacing from other community homes in the licensure file. The licensee rechecks it when a nearby community home opens or when the facility changes.

During an HHSC inspection or investigation, the manager gives surveyors access to the building, residents, staff, and records as the rules require. The manager notifies the licensee immediately. Staff do not obstruct and do not retaliate against anyone who talks to a surveyor.

The manager follows GOV-04 for any statement of violations. Informal dispute resolution under Subchapter G and enforcement remedies under Subchapter H are handled by the licensee. Deadlines in HHSC notices are entered on the compliance calendar on the day the notice is received.
The administrator reviews this policy annually and keeps a copy of the current licensing rules available to staff.

responsibilities.duty: Signs applications, pays fees, ensures renewal on time, and decides on disputes and enforcement responses.
Maintains the licensure file and compliance calendar, hosts surveys, and ensures building and capacity compliance.
Track deadlines and file submissions, receipts, and HHSC correspondence.

documentation: Current license and license history
TULIP submissions (Forms 3720 and 3721 as applicable) and confirmations
Local fire authority documentation and pre-licensure training certificate
LSC and health inspection reports
Fee payments (license fee, certification fee, added-bed fee, late fee, trust fund fee)
Renewal calendar
HHSC approval of capacity changes
Community-home zoning and spacing records (if applicable)
Survey, investigation, IDR, and enforcement correspondence

policies.title: Policy Review, Document Control and Rule Change Tracking
policies.applies_to: Manager, administrative staff, and all staff who use or are bound by facility policies at [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To keep the facility's policies and procedures current, controlled, and available, and to make sure residents are told of policy changes before they take effect. It also provides for tracking changes in HHSC rules.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains written resident policies and makes them available to staff and to residents or their responsible parties at admission. Residents are notified in writing of any policy change before its effective date. The emergency plan, evacuation summary, and contact lists are reviewed at least annually. They are also updated within 30 days after a disaster shortcoming, a drill shortcoming, or a change in facility policy or HHSC rule. The facility monitors HHSC rulemaking and updates citations when rules are adopted.

definitions.definition: The written policies that govern residents' care, rights, and responsibilities, which must be kept and given to residents or responsible parties at admission.
The date a new or revised policy begins to apply.
A rule published for comment that has not been adopted and does not yet bind the facility.

procedures: The manager keeps one controlled master copy of the Policy and Procedure Manual. Each policy shows its ID, title, effective date, and revision date.
Each policy is reviewed at least annually. The manager assigns reviewers, records the review date, and documents the changes made or that no change was needed.

A policy is also reviewed on any of these events: a change in HHSC rules, an inspection or survey finding, a significant incident, a change in services or license, or a change in the facility's operations.
The manager drafts revisions and the licensee approves them in writing. The approval date and effective date are entered on the revision log.
Written resident policies are available to all staff, and the manager makes them available to residents and responsible parties at admission. The admission checklist documents that this was done.

When a policy that affects residents changes, the manager notifies each resident or responsible party in writing before the change takes effect. Notice is delivered by hand or mail, and the date and method of delivery are documented. The manager does not enforce a changed policy against a resident before the notice is given.

Staff are told of each policy change within 7 days of approval, and the manager records each staff member's acknowledgment. Staff are trained on any change that affects resident care before it is put into practice.

The emergency plan, evacuation summary, and emergency contact lists are reviewed at least once a year. The manager also updates them within 30 days after a disaster shortcoming, a drill shortcoming, or a change in facility policy or HHSC rule. The review date and the changes made are documented.

The manager reviews the HHSC Chapter 553 rule pages and notices each month, and subscribes to HHSC provider updates. Rule changes are entered on a rule-change log with the source, adoption date, effective date, affected policies, and responsible person.

A proposed Chapter 553 revision (Proposed Rule 25R031, Texas Register, Sept. 4, 2026) would change on-duty staffing, add food handler and infection-control training, and renumber sections. It is proposed, not adopted. The manager follows the proposal and does not apply it until HHSC adopts it. On adoption, the manager updates affected policies (including STF-01, STF-03, DL-02 and SAF-07), corrects every citation, and gives notice of resident-facing changes under step 6.
Superseded versions are kept in an archive for at least the period required by REC-01 and marked 'superseded.' Only current versions are kept at the point of use.
The manager gives surveyors a complete current copy of the manual on request.

responsibilities.duty: Approves policy revisions and ensures resources to implement them.
Controls the manual, schedules reviews, notifies residents and staff, and maintains the rule-change log.
Reviews and updates the emergency plan within required timeframes.
Read and follow current policies and sign the acknowledgment of changes.

documentation: Master Policy and Procedure Manual with revision log
Annual review records
Resident notice of policy change with date and method of delivery
Admission checklist showing resident policies were provided
Staff acknowledgments of policy changes
Emergency plan review and update records
Rule-change log, including status of Proposed Rule 25R031
Archive of superseded policies

policies.title: Quality Assurance, Plans of Correction and Survey Response
policies.applies_to: Licensee, manager, and department leads at [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To provide a regular internal review of resident care and compliance and a consistent way to respond to HHSC inspection findings, plans of correction, and informal dispute resolution.
policies.policy: Chapter 553, as reviewed for this manual, does not prescribe a quality assurance and performance improvement (QAPI) program for ALFs. [AGENCY NAME] therefore adopts this policy voluntarily as a facility practice built on the review points the rules create. The manager reviews those points on a set schedule, corrects problems, and records the results. When HHSC cites a violation, the facility responds within the time allowed using HHSC's forms and follows the Subchapter G and H processes.

definitions.definition: The facility's written response to cited violations, submitted on HHSC Form 3724 (Statement of Licensing Violations and Plan of Correction).
HHSC Form 3614-A, used to document a contact with HHSC.
The process under Subchapter G for disputing cited violations.
The facility's periodic internal review of compliance and quality indicators.

procedures: The manager holds a QA review at least quarterly with the licensee and key staff. The date, attendees, findings, and assigned actions are recorded.

Each QA review looks at these points: drill shortcomings and whether each was corrected within 30 days; completion of annual resident assessments and service plan reviews, and plans due within 14 days of admission; trends in incident, accident, and abuse/neglect/exploitation reports; infection data; and resident grievances and how they were resolved.
For each problem found, the manager assigns an owner, a correction action, and a due date. Problems with resident safety are corrected immediately and not held for the next review.
Drill shortcomings found in a fire or emergency drill are corrected and the emergency plan updated within 30 days. The correction is recorded in the QA minutes and in the drill record.
When HHSC arrives for an inspection or investigation, staff direct the surveyor to the manager or backup manager, who notifies the licensee. Staff are polite and cooperative.
On receipt of a statement of violations, the manager records the date received and the response deadline on the compliance calendar the same day.

The manager prepares the plan of correction on HHSC Form 3724. For each cited violation the plan states what was done for the resident(s) affected, how other residents who might be affected are identified, what system change prevents a repeat, who is responsible, and the date of correction.
Placement-related submissions (HHSC Forms 1124, 1125 and 1126) are due within 10 working days of receiving them. The manager sends them within that period and keeps proof of delivery.
The licensee reviews and signs the plan of correction before it is submitted. A copy of what was submitted and the proof of the date submitted are filed.
Contacts with HHSC staff about a finding are recorded on Form 3614-A (Report of Contact) or in a dated contact log.
The manager verifies completion of every corrective action by the stated dates and documents the verification, including any follow-up audit. Staff are retrained where the cause was a training gap.

If the licensee disagrees with a finding, the licensee may request informal dispute resolution under Subchapter G within the time stated in HHSC's notice. The manager keeps the evidence supporting the dispute. Pursuing a dispute does not delay correction of any unsafe condition.
The licensee tracks any enforcement action under Subchapter H, including administrative penalties and license actions, with the notice date, deadlines, response, and outcome.
The most recent inspection report is posted as required in GOV-06. The manager reviews survey results at the next QA review and updates policies under GOV-03 as needed.

responsibilities.duty: Reviews QA findings, signs plans of correction, decides on disputes, and provides resources for correction.
Runs QA reviews, prepares and submits responses, verifies correction, and keeps survey records.
Carry out assigned corrective actions and provide information for QA reviews.

documentation: QA review minutes with action log
Statements of violations received
Plans of correction (Form 3724) and proof of submission date
Forms 3614-A and contact logs
Placement forms 1124, 1125, 1126 and proof of timely submission
Verification of correction records and follow-up audits
IDR requests and decisions
Enforcement notices and responses

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
policies.applies_to: Licensee, manager, billing and administrative staff, and all employees and contractors of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To prevent fraud, waste, and abuse and to make sure all charges to residents, managed care organizations (MCOs), and payers are accurate and lawful. It also keeps the facility free of excluded persons and meets the requirements of its Medicaid managed care participation.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] bills only for services actually delivered and documented, uses the correct billing codes, and never offers or accepts payment in exchange for referrals. The facility screens owners, controlling persons, employees, and contractors against exclusion lists and does not employ or contract with excluded persons. As a STAR+PLUS HCBS assisted living provider, it is screened and enrolled and contracts with MCOs. It follows each MCO's billing guide and keeps financial records of charges as the rules require.

definitions.definition: A person or entity excluded from participation in Medicare, Medicaid, or other federal health care programs.
A claim for payment the facility knows is false, including billing for services not provided or at a higher level than supported.
The billing code for STAR+PLUS assisted living services, billed at the level that matches the member's approved service level.
The amount a STAR+PLUS member pays the facility for housing and meals. It can be reduced but not waived.
Anything of value offered, paid, or received to induce or reward referrals of federal health care program business.

procedures: The licensee designates the manager as the compliance contact. All staff are told they may report compliance concerns to the compliance contact or, if the concern involves the manager, directly to the licensee at [PHONE]. Reports may be made anonymously and no one is retaliated against for a good faith report.

Before an initial license application, the licensee confirms that the applicant and controlling persons are not excluded from Medicare/Medicaid and have no license revoked in the past 5 years. HHSC must deny a license in either case.

Before hire or contracting, and at least monthly after that, the manager checks every employee and contractor against the federal and Texas exclusion lists and documents the date and result. A person found excluded is removed from duties at once and the licensee is informed. Exclusion screening is coordinated with STF-02.

The facility keeps its STAR+PLUS provider screening and enrollment current and contracts only with MCOs it is eligible to serve. Members are admitted only under the housing option stated in the MCO contract (apartment or non-apartment).

Billing staff bill HCPCS T2031 at the level code authorized by the MCO. Staff verify the authorization and each MCO's billing guide before billing. They check that the member's service plan and daily documentation support the billed level and days.

No claim is submitted for a day when the member was not in the facility, for services not provided, or at an unsupported level. The manager reviews a sample of claims against records at least quarterly.

The facility keeps a simple financial record of the charges billed to each resident, and a record of any personal funds the facility handles, available to HHSC. Receipts are issued on request. Resident funds are handled under RR-05.

The facility may reduce room and board for a STAR+PLUS member but may not waive it. The amount is prorated in the first month and due on a written date stated in the admission agreement. The facility keeps member trust fund records as required by the Handbook. See RR-04.

The facility does not offer, pay, solicit, or accept anything of value for referrals. Marketing arrangements, gifts to referral sources, and any discounts are reviewed by the licensee before they are used.

The facility's operations for STAR+PLUS members follow the HCBS setting requirements of 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4), including resident choice, privacy, and freedom to receive visitors. Conflicts with house rules are corrected.

Billing errors are corrected promptly. Any overpayment is reported and returned to the payer within the time the payer or law requires. The facility documents the discovery, the amount, and the date returned.
The manager trains all staff on this policy at orientation and annually. The training covers the False Claims Act, the Anti-Kickback law, documentation accuracy, and how to report concerns.
The licensee reviews compliance reports at the quarterly QA review under GOV-04 and records actions taken.

responsibilities.duty: Sets the compliance expectation, approves marketing and referral arrangements, and ensures overpayments are returned.
Acts as compliance contact, runs exclusion screening and claim reviews, and trains staff.
Bill accurately using authorized levels and keep financial records.
Document accurately and report suspected fraud or billing problems.

documentation: Exclusion screening results for owners, staff and contractors with dates
STAR+PLUS/MCO contracts, screening and enrollment records
MCO authorizations and billing guides
Claims and supporting daily documentation
Quarterly claim review records
Resident financial records and receipts
Member trust fund records
Room and board agreements
Overpayment return records
Compliance training attendance and compliance reports

policies.title: Required Postings and Providers' Bill of Rights
policies.applies_to: Manager and administrative staff of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] posts every notice required by HHSC where residents, employees, and visitors can see it, honors the Providers' Bill of Rights, and uses only accurate advertising.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] posts all required notices in a public area readily available to residents, employees, and visitors, and keeps them current. It posts the Residents' Bill of Rights in each resident's primary language. It posts the Providers' Bill of Rights and the electronic monitoring notice. Advertising and promotional material comply with §553.272, and the Memory Care Disclosure Statement is given whenever memory care is marketed.

definitions.definition: A location in the facility readily available to residents, employees, and visitors, such as the entrance or main lobby.
The normal staffing plan for all shifts over a 24-hour day, which is disclosed before admission and posted.

The statement of the rights of an ALF provider, including the right to terminate a resident agreement for just cause on 30 days' written notice, or immediately for a serious threat after notice to HHSC at 1-800-458-9858.
The disclosure given to residents and responsible parties when the facility markets memory care services.

procedures: The manager keeps a posting checklist and assigns one person to verify the postings weekly. The checklist lists each notice, its location, and the date it was last verified.

The facility posts, in a public area readily available to residents, employees and visitors: (1) the license; (2) the HHSC complaint-procedure sign; (3) the notice that inspection reports are available, with the HHSC toll-free number; (4) the most recent inspection report; (5) the Residents' Bill of Rights; (6) the Providers' Bill of Rights; (7) the local ombudsman number and the toll-free number 1-800-252-2412; (8) the normal 24-hour staffing pattern; and (9) the sign 'Cases of Suspected Abuse, Neglect, or Exploitation must be reported to HHSC by calling 1-800-458-9858.'

The Residents' Bill of Rights is posted in each resident's primary language. The manager asks each resident or responsible party for the primary language at admission and obtains and posts the translation if needed. See RR-08.
The manager updates the posted staffing pattern each month and records the update date. The staffing pattern matches the actual staffing in STF-01 and is disclosed to residents before admission.
When HHSC issues a new inspection report, the manager replaces the posted report with it within 2 business days and documents the date.
When the license is renewed, the manager replaces the posted license on the day received.
The manager posts the 8½ x 11 'Electronic Monitoring' notice at the main entrance as required for authorized electronic monitoring. See RR-09.

The facility honors the Providers' Bill of Rights. The manager follows the 30-day written notice for termination for just cause, or immediate termination for a serious threat only after notice to HHSC at 1-800-458-9858. All discharges are handled under ADM-06.

Before any advertisement, brochure, website text, social media post, or promotional material is used, the manager reviews it against the current text of §553.272. The review is documented. The manager does not approve material that states services, licensure status, staffing, or pricing the facility does not actually provide.

If the facility markets memory care, the manager gives the Memory Care Disclosure Statement to each prospective resident or responsible party before admission and documents the date it was given. See HCS-06 and ADM-01.
The manager keeps a file of all approved advertisements and the date each was reviewed. Outdated material is withdrawn.
During the weekly checks the manager also confirms the postings are not covered, damaged, or outdated. Missing items are replaced the same day.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures all postings are present and current and approves advertising.
Performs weekly posting checks and updates the monthly staffing pattern.
Ensures resources to obtain translations and required notices and does not approve non-compliant marketing.

documentation: Posting checklist with weekly verification dates
Posted staffing pattern with monthly update record
Record of primary-language translations of the Residents' Bill of Rights
Record of inspection report and license replacement dates
Advertising review file with approval dates
Memory Care Disclosure Statement delivery record, if memory care is marketed

policies.title: Resident Rights and Responsibilities (Residents' Bill of Rights)
policies.applies_to: All [AGENCY NAME] staff, contractors and volunteers; all residents and their legal representatives
policies.purpose: To make sure every resident knows, receives and can exercise the rights guaranteed by the Texas Residents' Bill of Rights, and that staff honor those rights every day.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] gives every resident a copy of the Residents' Bill of Rights at admission, posts it in a public area in each resident's primary language, and operates in a way that protects those rights. Residents may complain without reprisal; be free from abuse and from restraint used for discipline or convenience; receive unopened mail; have visitors at any reasonable hour; use a telephone and have privacy; choose their own physician; take part in service planning; refuse treatment; keep a locked personal area; manage their own finances with an accounting at least quarterly; see their records; and leave the facility temporarily or permanently. Restraint is used only on written physician authorization or in an emergency. Residents are told by the 30th day after admission whether they are entitled to Medicare or Medicaid benefits and which items and services are covered. A married couple receiving similar services may share a room if they choose. Residents are also expected to follow the written resident policies and to respect the rights of other residents and staff. A resident's failure to meet these responsibilities is addressed under ADM-06 and does not remove the resident's rights.

definitions.definition: The list of resident rights required by Texas rule (26 TAC §553.267), which the facility must give to each resident and post.
A guardian, agent under a power of attorney, or other person with legal authority to act for a resident.
The language the resident uses and best understands.
Any retaliation or discrimination against a resident or other person for making a complaint or exercising a right.

procedures: Before admission, the Administrator or designee gives the resident or legal representative the facility disclosure statement and a copy of the Residents' Bill of Rights, and explains them in plain language.
At admission, the admitting staff member reviews each right with the resident, answers questions, and confirms understanding using interpreter or accessible-format support where needed (see RR-08).

The resident or legal representative signs an acknowledgment of receipt; staff file it in the resident record the same day. If the resident declines to sign, staff note the date, who explained the rights and the refusal.
The Administrator posts the Residents' Bill of Rights in a public area, in each resident's primary language, and checks monthly that it is present and legible. Postings are logged under GOV-06.

By the 30th day after admission, the Administrator or designee gives the resident written notice of whether the resident is entitled to Medicare or Medicaid benefits and which items and services are covered, and documents the date given.
Staff protect mail privacy: all incoming and outgoing mail is delivered unopened unless the resident asks for help. Staff may not read, hold or screen mail.
Staff allow visitors at any reasonable hour. Any limit a resident requests on visitors is recorded in the service plan; the facility does not impose limits on its own except as allowed under SAF-08.
Staff provide access to a telephone and a private place for calls, and respect the resident's privacy during personal care, visits and calls.
Each resident is offered a lockable area in the living quarters for valuables. Staff do not enter it without the resident's permission except in an emergency.

Staff respect each resident's choice of physician and right to refuse treatment. Staff report a refusal to the resident's physician and record it under HCS-05 so the resident can make an informed choice.
Residents are invited to take part in developing and updating their own service plan (see ADM-03). Staff document who attended and the resident's preferences.
No restraint may be used for discipline or convenience. Restraint is used only as in SAF-04: on written physician authorization or in an emergency.

Staff do not discriminate against or retaliate against any resident or person acting for a resident who complains or exercises a right. Suspected retaliation is reported to the Administrator immediately.

Staff who see or are told of a possible rights violation report it to the Administrator the same shift. The Administrator reviews it, takes corrective action and documents it. Allegations of abuse, neglect or exploitation follow SAF-01.
Married couples who ask to share a room and who receive similar services are accommodated when space allows; the choice is documented in both records.
The Administrator provides rights training to every new employee at orientation and annually thereafter (see STF-03), and reviews rights complaints at each quality assurance meeting (see GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures the Bill of Rights is given, posted and honored; reviews rights complaints; ensures no reprisal.
Reviews and delivers the Bill of Rights, obtains the signed acknowledgment, and files it.
Honor each right in daily care and report suspected violations immediately.
Follow the written resident policies and respect the rights of others.

documentation: Signed acknowledgment of receipt of the Residents' Bill of Rights
Documentation of the Medicare/Medicaid entitlement notice given by day 30
Posting verification log
Staff rights training records
Rights violation reviews and corrective action notes

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
policies.applies_to: All [AGENCY NAME] staff; all residents, legal representatives and families
policies.purpose: To give residents an easy, safe way to raise concerns about care or treatment and to make sure each concern is answered promptly and without reprisal.
policies.policy: A resident may complain about care or treatment, in person, in writing, anonymously or through a designee, without fear of retaliation. [AGENCY NAME] responds promptly to every complaint and does not discriminate or retaliate against anyone who complains. The facility posts the HHSC complaint-procedure sign and the HHSC toll-free number so residents can go directly to the state at any time, and a resident is never required to use the internal process first. Complaints that allege abuse, neglect or exploitation are not handled as internal grievances. They are reported and investigated under SAF-01.

definitions.definition: Any complaint or concern raised by or for a resident about care, treatment, services, staff or other residents.
A person a resident chooses to raise or follow a complaint on the resident's behalf.
Any adverse action, threat or discrimination because someone made a complaint or took part in an investigation.
The HHSC toll-free line (1-800-458-9858) that receives complaints and reports about licensed facilities.

procedures: At admission, staff explain to the resident how to make a complaint to any staff member, the Administrator ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME], [PHONE]), the local ombudsman, or HHSC, and note the discussion in the record.
The Administrator posts the HHSC complaint-procedure sign, the HHSC toll-free number and the ombudsman numbers in a public area, and checks them monthly (see GOV-06).
The facility makes complaint forms and a locked or private drop box available so residents may complain in writing or anonymously. The Administrator checks the box at least weekly.

Any staff member who receives a complaint, verbal or written, writes down the date, time, resident name (unless anonymous), the complaint and who received it, and gives it to the Administrator by the end of the shift.

Before logging a complaint as a grievance, staff screen it. If it alleges abuse, neglect or exploitation, staff stop the grievance process and follow SAF-01, including the immediate report to HHSC at 1-800-458-9858 and to law enforcement.
If the complaint involves an immediate risk to health or safety, staff act at once to protect the resident and notify the Administrator or on-call manager immediately.
The Administrator acknowledges the complaint with the resident or designee promptly, and in any case by the next business day, and tells the resident who is handling it.
The Administrator investigates by speaking with the resident, staff and any witnesses, and reviewing records. Staff involved are not allowed to investigate their own conduct.

The Administrator gives the resident or designee a prompt response explaining what was found and what will be done. For anonymous complaints, the Administrator posts a general response or addresses the issue in a resident meeting without identifying anyone.
If the concern requires a change of care, the Administrator or Nurse updates the service plan under ADM-03 and tells the resident's physician or representative as needed.
The Administrator reminds the resident that the resident may take the complaint to the local ombudsman or HHSC at any time, regardless of the outcome of the internal response.

The Administrator monitors the resident for signs of retaliation or discrimination for a reasonable time after the complaint and documents the follow-up. Staff found to have retaliated are disciplined under STF-07.
The Administrator enters each complaint, finding and response in the grievance log and reviews the log for trends at every quality assurance meeting (see GOV-04).
During an HHSC survey, the Administrator makes the grievance log available and cooperates fully with any complaint investigation (see GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Owns the grievance process, investigates, responds promptly, prevents retaliation and reviews trends.
Accept any complaint without discouragement, record it and pass it on by end of shift; report abuse, neglect or exploitation under SAF-01.
Review care-related complaints and update the service plan as needed.

documentation: Grievance log with dates, findings, responses and follow-up
Written complaint forms and notes of verbal complaints
Posting verification log for complaint signage
Records of retaliation follow-up checks
Quality assurance meeting minutes showing grievance trend review

policies.title: Ombudsman Access
policies.applies_to: All [AGENCY NAME] staff, especially the Administrator, receptionist and charge staff
policies.purpose: To make sure the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program has immediate, private and unimpeded access to residents and records so residents can get advocacy help.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] allows the State Ombudsman, certified ombudsmen and ombudsman interns immediate, private, unimpeded access to the facility and to residents during regular business or visiting hours. The State Ombudsman and certified ombudsmen may also enter at other times if circumstances require. Residents have the right to communicate privately with an ombudsman. The facility releases resident records to the ombudsman with the resident's consent or as the Texas ombudsman access rule otherwise allows. The ombudsman is a health oversight agency, so HIPAA does not bar release. The facility posts the local ombudsman number and the toll-free number, 1-800-252-2412, and never obstructs, delays or retaliates for ombudsman contact.

definitions.definition: The state official, and the certified ombudsmen and interns who work under that office, who advocate for residents of long-term care facilities.
A trained, certified representative of the State Ombudsman Program.
An agency authorized by law to oversee the health care system; HIPAA permits disclosure of health information to it.
Entry and contact with residents without requiring advance notice, escort, a delay or staff presence.

procedures: The Administrator posts the local ombudsman telephone number and 1-800-252-2412 in a public area, and checks them monthly (see GOV-06).
At admission, staff tell each resident and legal representative about the ombudsman program and give the contact numbers; the discussion is noted in the record.
All staff are trained at orientation (see STF-03) to recognize an ombudsman and to admit them immediately. Staff do not require an appointment or advance notice.

When an ombudsman arrives, the first staff member on duty checks the visitor's identification or badge and notes the visitor's name and time of arrival in the visitor log, then notifies the Administrator or manager on duty without delaying entry.
Staff allow the ombudsman to go to residents' rooms and common areas and to speak with any resident who is willing, in private. Staff do not accompany the ombudsman unless the ombudsman asks.

If an ombudsman asks to enter outside business or visiting hours and says circumstances require it, the person in charge allows access if the visitor is the State Ombudsman or a certified ombudsman, and calls the Administrator after entry.
Staff respect the resident's choice. A resident may decline to meet an ombudsman, and staff may not pressure or discourage a resident from meeting one.

When an ombudsman asks to review a resident's record, the Administrator or designee checks whether the resident or legal representative has consented, or whether the access rule otherwise allows access, and provides the record the same day if possible.
Staff do not refuse a records request because of HIPAA concerns. If staff are unsure, they immediately contact the Administrator, who confirms the basis for release and records it.
The Administrator provides a private space for ombudsman interviews and records review, and gives the ombudsman reasonable assistance, such as copies, at no charge.
Staff do not read, edit or remove records before an ombudsman review, and do not tell residents what they may or may not say.
The Administrator logs each ombudsman visit and records request in the ombudsman contact log (date, ombudsman name, purpose and records released).
The Administrator investigates and responds to any issue the ombudsman raises, as in RR-02, and corrects any problem found.
Any staff member who delays, obstructs or retaliates because of ombudsman contact is disciplined under STF-07, and the Administrator documents the corrective action.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures access policy is followed, authorizes records release, posts numbers and resolves concerns raised.
Admits the ombudsman immediately, logs the visit and notifies the Administrator.
Do not impede, discourage or retaliate; refer records requests to the Administrator.

documentation: Ombudsman contact and visit log
Records release log noting consent or legal basis
Posting verification log
Orientation training records on ombudsman access
Follow-up notes on issues raised by the ombudsman

policies.title: Admission Agreement, Fees, Deposits and Refunds
policies.applies_to: Administrator, admissions and business office staff; all prospective residents and legal representatives
policies.purpose: To make sure each resident has a clear written agreement that states services and charges, receives required disclosures before admission, and is protected in the handling of fees, deposits, refunds and termination.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] uses a written admission agreement for every resident that states the services provided and the charges. Before admission, the facility gives the resident or legal representative the disclosure statement and rate schedule and documents receipt. If any service or supply could be a Medicare benefit, the resident receives a written statement saying so. Written resident policies cover the residents the facility accepts, services, charges, refunds, responsibilities, privileges and rules, and the facility gives notice of changes before they take effect. The facility may terminate an agreement only for just cause and on 30 days' written notice, or immediately for a serious or immediate threat after notice to HHSC. For STAR+PLUS HCBS residents, room and board is limited to the Medicaid-set amount, may not be waived (a lower amount may be accepted), is prorated in the first month and is due on a written date.

definitions.definition: The signed written contract between the facility and the resident that states services, charges and responsibilities.
The written statement of facility services, staffing and rates that must be given before admission.
The written list of the facility's charges for room, board, services and supplies.
The monthly amount the Medicaid member pays the facility, limited to the SSI rate minus the $85 personal needs allowance ($909 per month in 2026).
A reason for termination that is allowed by the Texas rule and written in the admission agreement.

procedures: During the first inquiry, admissions staff give the prospective resident the rate schedule and explain which services are included and which cost extra.

Before admission, the Administrator gives the resident or legal representative the disclosure statement, rate schedule and written resident policies, reviews them, and records the date given and the signature of the recipient.

Admissions staff prepare the written admission agreement stating services, charges, the date payment is due, refund terms, responsibilities, privileges, rules and the grounds for termination. The Administrator reviews it before signing.
If any service or supply could be a Medicare benefit, the Administrator adds the required written statement saying so to the agreement or its attachment.
The resident or legal representative signs the agreement and receives a copy. Staff place the signed original in the resident record. The resident is not asked to sign a blank or incomplete form.

For STAR+PLUS residents, admissions staff confirm the resident's managed care organization (MCO) contract status and the housing option (apartment or non-apartment) stated in the MCO contract before admission (see ADM-07).

For STAR+PLUS residents, the business office sets room and board no higher than the Medicaid limit ($909 per month in 2026), does not waive it, may accept a lower amount if the resident can pay only that, prorates it for the first month and states the due date in writing.

Any deposit or other prepaid amount is stated in the agreement with the conditions for refund. The business office issues a written receipt for each payment on request and records it in the resident's financial record.
At move-out or discharge, the business office calculates the final charges, prorates amounts to the last day of residence, and refunds any amount due within the time stated in the agreement.

Before any rate, service or policy change takes effect, the Administrator gives each affected resident written notice and records delivery. Changes do not apply to a resident before the notice has been given.
By the 30th day after admission, the facility gives each resident the written Medicare/Medicaid entitlement notice (see RR-01).

The Administrator may terminate an admission agreement only for just cause and on 30 days' written notice, following ADM-06. The notice states the reason and tells the resident about the ombudsman and appeal rights.

If a resident presents a serious or immediate threat to the health or safety of others, the Administrator may terminate immediately, but must first notify HHSC by calling 1-800-458-9858 (the number to use on evenings, weekends and holidays), and must document the call.
The Administrator reviews the agreement, rate schedule and disclosure statement at least annually and whenever a rule changes (see GOV-03), and updates them before new admissions.

responsibilities.duty: Approves agreements, rate schedules and disclosures; makes termination decisions and required notices to HHSC.
Prepare and explain agreements; collect, receipt and record payments and refunds.
Review and sign the agreement and pay charges on the written due date.

documentation: Signed admission agreement
Signed receipt of disclosure statement, rate schedule and written resident policies
Medicare benefit statement, where applicable
Receipts, ledgers and deposit/refund records
Notices of change and 30-day termination notices; record of HHSC call for immediate termination
STAR+PLUS room and board calculation and due date

policies.title: Resident Funds and Personal Property
policies.applies_to: Administrator, business office staff and all staff who handle or may be responsible for resident money or belongings
policies.purpose: To protect each resident's right to manage his or her own money and belongings and to make sure any funds the facility handles are safeguarded and accurately recorded.
policies.policy: Residents may manage their own money or authorize another person in writing to do so. The resident chooses how funds are managed (for example a money management program, representative payee, financial power of attorney or trust) and may choose the least restrictive method. [AGENCY NAME] accepts responsibility for a resident's funds only on the resident's written delegation. When it does, it gives the resident an accounting at least quarterly and on request. The facility keeps a simple financial record of receipts and expenditures, which is available to HHSC, and issues receipts for payments on request. Residents keep and use their personal property and have a locked area in their living quarters. For STAR+PLUS residents, member trust fund records are kept as the STAR+PLUS Handbook requires. Staff never borrow from, accept gifts from, or use a resident's money or property.

definitions.definition: Money belonging to a resident, including a personal needs allowance, that is held or managed for the resident.
A signed authorization from the resident (or legal representative) allowing the facility to hold or handle funds.
The account and records the facility keeps for a STAR+PLUS member's funds that it holds.
Clothing, furnishings, valuables and other items that belong to the resident.

procedures: At admission, the Administrator or designee asks each resident how the resident wishes to manage money and records the resident's choice, including any representative payee, agent or trustee.
