documentation: Medication storage designation and key/code list
Medication profile records and receipt logs
Refrigerator temperature log
Controlled drug count log (if controlled drugs are stored)
Monthly medication storage inspection records
Disposal records signed by the pharmacist
Discharge medication release receipts
Discrepancy and loss reports

policies.title: Medication Administration and Staff Authorization
policies.applies_to: Administrator/Manager, Nurse, medication aides, RN-delegated employees, and all staff who may administer medications at [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure medications are given to residents only by people legally authorized to do so, according to physician orders, and that each dose is properly recorded.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] administers medications only according to physician orders. For a resident who cannot or chooses not to self-administer, medications are given only by: (i) a currently licensed person authorized to administer medications; (ii) a medication aide with a current permit, acting under a licensed nurse who is on duty or on call; or (iii) an employee delegated by a registered nurse under the Texas Board of Nursing delegation rules (§553.261(a)(1)(A)). A nurse is employed by or on call to the facility. If the facility does not have a nurse employed or on call, it admits only residents who self-administer their medications. Staff keep a medication profile record for each resident and document every missed or refused dose.

definitions.definition: A person who holds a current Texas medication aide permit, which requires 100 classroom hours, 20 lab hours, 10 clinical hours, and an exam, and is renewed annually.
A registered nurse's assignment of a specific task to a trained employee, with instruction and supervision, under Texas Board of Nursing rules.
A record for each resident showing each medication's name, strength, dosage, amount received, directions, route, prescription number, pharmacy, and date issued.
Available by phone and able to respond when needed, with the contact information posted for medication staff.
A dose not given at the ordered time or within the ordered window.
A dose the resident declines to take.

procedures: The Administrator makes sure a licensed nurse is employed by or on call to the facility. The facility uses [NURSE NAME/AGENCY] for this role. The Administrator posts the nurse's name and phone number where medication staff can find it.

The Administrator plans nurse hours based on the number of residents and their needs. As an operator estimate (not a regulatory requirement), a 6-bed home may plan about 4 hours per week and a 16-bed facility about 8 hours per week, adjusted to resident acuity and how many residents need medication administration.

If the facility does not have a nurse employed or on call at any time, the Administrator admits only residents who self-administer under HCS-03. The Administrator does not allow unauthorized staff to administer medications.

The Administrator keeps a list of everyone authorized to administer medications. The list shows each person's status: licensed nurse, permitted medication aide, or RN-delegated employee. For each, the Administrator verifies the license or permit and records the expiration date.

For a medication aide, the Administrator verifies the Texas permit before the first shift and confirms that the aide is working under a licensed nurse who is on duty or on call. The permit is renewed every year ($15). After the first renewal, 7 hours of continuing education are required, and the Administrator tracks completion and expiration dates.

For an RN-delegated employee, the RN assesses the resident and the employee, delegates the task in writing under the Board of Nursing rules, trains the employee, and supervises. The Administrator keeps the delegation records in the personnel file (STF-06).

Only a physician's order, written or verbal and recorded, is used to give a medication. The Nurse checks every new or changed order against the medication profile and the pharmacy label before the first dose.
The Nurse creates and maintains a medication profile record for each resident. It records name, strength, dosage, amount received, directions, route, prescription number, pharmacy, and date issued.

Before each dose, the authorized staff member checks the resident's identity and the medication against the order and profile, gives the medication, and immediately records the date, time, and initials on the medication administration record.

If a resident shows an unusual reaction to a medication, staff stop the medication if safe and instructed to do so, call the Nurse, and immediately report the reaction to the physician and responsible party. Staff document the reaction, the notice, and the physician's response (HCS-05).

For every missed or refused dose, staff record the date, time, and medication name and strength. Staff do not document when the resident is away from the facility. Staff notify the Nurse of repeated refusals. The Nurse informs the physician.

Medication errors are reported to the Nurse and Administrator at once. The Nurse contacts the physician, monitors the resident, and documents the error and the response. The Administrator reviews errors for trends (SAF-02, GOV-04).
The Nurse reviews the administration records at least monthly, checks for gaps and errors, and checks that orders match the profile. The Nurse reports findings to the Administrator.

Staff who give medications complete orientation and ongoing training required under STF-03. The Administrator may remove a person's authorization if there are repeated errors, an expired permit, or a lack of supervision.

responsibilities.duty: Makes sure a nurse is employed or on call, maintains the authorized-staff list, verifies licenses and permits, and removes authorization when needed.
Supervises medication aides, delegates tasks as an RN where applicable, maintains medication profiles, reviews orders and records, and responds to reactions and errors.
Holds a current permit, works under a nurse on duty or on call, administers medications as ordered, and documents each dose, missed dose, and refusal.
Performs only the delegated tasks as instructed and reports questions or changes to the delegating RN.
Writes orders and responds to reports of reactions and refusals.

documentation: List of staff authorized to administer medications, with license, permit, and delegation verification and expiration dates
Nurse employment or on-call agreement and posted contact information
Medication profile record for each resident
Physician orders
Medication administration records, including missed and refused dose entries
Reaction and error reports with physician and representative notification
RN delegation records and training
Monthly medication record review notes

policies.title: Medication Supervision and Resident Self-Administration
policies.applies_to: Administrator/Manager, attendants and other staff who supervise residents' medications, the consulting nurse, and residents who self-administer
policies.purpose: To set out how [AGENCY NAME] supervises residents who take their own medications, keeps those medications secure, and checks regularly that self-administration is still safe. The policy applies the medication supervision and self-administration requirements of 26 TAC §553.261(a) and HHSC Provider Letter 2023-22.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] limits medication supervision to the tasks the rule allows: reminders; opening containers and replacing lids; pouring the prescribed dose according to the medication profile; returning medications to locked storage; obtaining medications from the pharmacy; and maintaining the medication profile record. The resident, not staff, takes the medication. Staff do not place medication in a resident's mouth, apply or inject it, or otherwise give it to a resident who cannot take it independently. That is medication administration and may be done only as described in HCS-02. A resident who keeps medications locked in his or her room is counseled by staff at least monthly on whether he or she can still self-administer safely and keep the medications secure, and each counseling is recorded in writing. A resident may enter the central storage area to self-administer only while a staff member is present the whole time.

definitions.definition: Limited assistance that lets a resident who can take his or her own medication do so: reminders, opening containers and replacing lids, pouring the prescribed dose per the medication profile, returning medications to locked storage, obtaining medications from the pharmacy, and keeping the medication profile record.
The resident takes or applies his or her own medication, with or without supervision as defined above.

Any act beyond supervision that gives a medication to a resident. It may be done only by a licensed nurse, a permitted medication aide working under a nurse on duty or on call, or an employee delegated by an RN (see HCS-02).
The facility's written record for each resident of the prescribed medications, doses, times and routes, and the resident's supervised or self-administered doses.
The locked storage area where the facility keeps residents' medications that are not kept in the resident's room (see HCS-01).

procedures: At admission and at each assessment, the Administrator or designee and the consulting nurse review the resident's physician orders, cognition, vision, dexterity and history of medication use to decide whether the resident can self-administer with supervision. The determination is entered in the assessment and service plan (ADM-02, ADM-03).

If the resident cannot reliably take his or her own medications even with supervision, the resident's medications are handled as administration under HCS-02, and the service plan and admission agreement are updated. If the facility cannot meet the resident's medication needs, the Administrator follows ADM-04 and ADM-05.

The Administrator or designee ensures that each resident who self-administers has a current medication profile record. It is updated whenever the physician changes an order and when a new prescription is obtained.

Staff who supervise medications are trained in these limits during orientation and on-the-job training (STF-03). The Administrator assigns supervision tasks only to staff who have completed that training.
Staff provide reminders at the scheduled times. The resident decides whether to take the dose, and a refusal is recorded and reported under step 11.

Staff may open containers and replace lids and may pour the prescribed dose, reading the dose from the medication profile record and the pharmacy label. Staff do not change a dose, split or crush medications, or give a dose that does not match the profile and label.
Staff hand the poured dose to the resident, who takes it. Staff record on the medication profile record that supervision was given and the date and time.
Staff return medications to locked storage immediately after use. Medications are never left unattended on counters, in carts or in common areas.

A staff member or designated person obtains medications from the pharmacy. The person receiving them checks them against the order and the medication profile record. Discrepancies are reported to the pharmacy and the physician before the medication is used.

For a resident who keeps medications locked in his or her room, the Administrator ensures that a lockable container or drawer is provided and that the resident or representative agrees to the arrangement in writing. The resident controls the key, and the facility keeps a plan for emergency access.

At least once a month, a staff member counsels each such resident on whether he or she can still self-administer safely and keep the medications secure. The counseling covers missed or doubled doses, confusion about medications, who has access to the room, and storage. The staff member writes up the counseling and signs and dates it.

If the counseling shows that the resident can no longer self-administer safely or secure the medications, the staff member notifies the Administrator the same day. The Administrator moves the medications to central storage, notifies the consulting nurse, the physician and the resident's representative, and updates the service plan.

A resident who wishes to take medications from central storage is accompanied by a staff member who stays present the entire time the resident is in the storage area. The resident does not remove other residents' medications or leave the area with unsupervised access.

Staff report to the physician and the responsible party immediately any unusual reaction to a medication, and follow HCS-05. Refusals, missed doses and medication errors are reported to the Administrator and documented. The Administrator reviews them with the consulting nurse and the physician as needed.
Medications of a discharged or deceased resident are disposed of or returned under HCS-01 and HCS-10, and the disposition is documented.
The Administrator reviews medication supervision records and monthly counseling records at least quarterly as part of quality assurance (GOV-04) and corrects any gaps.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures only trained staff supervise medications, that monthly counseling is done and recorded, and that medication supervision records are reviewed and kept.
Perform only the allowed supervision tasks, document each one, return medications to locked storage, and report refusals, reactions and concerns immediately.
Helps determine whether a resident can self-administer, reviews concerns from monthly counseling, and advises on changes to the service plan.
Takes the medication as prescribed, keeps medications secure if they are stored in the room, and tells staff about problems or changes.

documentation: Medication profile record for each resident
Written record of monthly counseling for residents who keep medications in their rooms
Written agreement for in-room storage and the plan for emergency access
Assessment and service plan entries on self-administration ability
Staff training records on medication supervision limits
Records of refusals, reactions and errors, and notifications of the physician and responsible party

policies.title: Nursing Services, RN Delegation and Health Maintenance Activities
policies.applies_to: Administrator/Manager, registered nurse (employed or contracted), personal care staff, outside health professionals and HCSSA providers, residents and representatives
federal: 22 TAC Chapter 225 (RN delegation), as referenced in 26 TAC §553.263 and §553.261(a)(1)(A)(iii)
policies.purpose: To define how [AGENCY NAME] allows health care professionals to serve residents without providing ongoing nursing-facility-level care, and how it uses health maintenance activities (HMAs) and RN delegation for tasks that go beyond personal care.
policies.policy: Health care professionals may coordinate services for residents within their scope of practice, but [AGENCY NAME] does not provide ongoing services comparable to those of a nursing facility. A resident may contract with a licensed home and community support services agency (HCSSA) or an independent health professional for nursing or therapy services. Services for temporary illness or injury may be delivered by qualified persons. Personal care staff perform an HMA without delegation only when an RN has assessed and documented that the task qualifies: the resident has a functional disability, the condition is stable and predictable, and the resident or representative is able and willing to direct the task and agrees in writing. A task that is not an HMA, including any medication administration, may be done by personal care staff only through RN delegation under 22 TAC Chapter 225 and, for medication, the delegation requirements described in HCS-02. The RN reassesses an HMA on any change of condition, at least annually, and at least every 6 months for a resident with Alzheimer's disease or a related disorder or a resident in a certified facility or unit.

definitions.definition: A task that goes beyond ordinary personal care but that personal care staff may perform without delegation when an RN has assessed and documented that it qualifies under §553.263.
An RN's assignment of a nursing task to an unlicensed person under 22 TAC Chapter 225 when the task is not an HMA.
A licensed home and community support services agency that a resident may contract with to provide services in the facility.
Continuing skilled care of the type a nursing facility provides, which the facility may not provide on an ongoing basis.
A condition that the RN documents as not changing in a way that requires frequent reassessment or nursing judgment.

procedures: The Administrator designates a registered nurse, [RN NAME / CONTRACTED RN AGENCY], who is responsible for HMA assessments and delegation decisions. The RN's license is verified at engagement and each renewal (STF-06).

When a resident has a need that goes beyond personal care, the Administrator or designee refers the need to the RN within one business day. No staff member performs the task until the RN has made a written determination.

The RN determines whether the task qualifies as an HMA. The RN confirms the resident has a functional disability, the condition is stable and predictable, and the resident or representative can direct the task. The assessment is documented in the resident's record.

The resident or representative gives written agreement that personal care staff may perform the HMA and that the resident or representative will direct the task. The agreement is signed and dated and filed with the RN assessment.
The RN identifies the staff members who may perform the HMA, trains them, checks their competence, and records the training. Staff do not perform an HMA until they have been trained.
The task and who may perform it are added to the resident's service plan (ADM-03). Staff perform the HMA as directed by the resident or representative and document each time it is done.

If the task is not an HMA, the RN decides whether delegation under 22 TAC Chapter 225 is appropriate. If the RN delegates, the RN documents the delegation, instructs and supervises the staff member as required by the rule, and records the training. Medication tasks follow HCS-02.

If the task cannot be an HMA and the RN will not delegate it, no facility staff member performs it. The Administrator tells the resident and representative, and the resident may arrange for an HCSSA or an independent health professional. If the need cannot be met in this way, the Administrator reviews it under ADM-04 and ADM-05.

The Administrator checks that every HCSSA or independent professional serving a resident is under a written agreement with the resident, and obtains the provider's name, contact information and the date services began. The provider's care plan is coordinated with the facility's service plan.

For services for temporary illness or injury, the Administrator confirms that the person delivering them is qualified, records the expected duration, and reviews the arrangement with the RN. If the need becomes ongoing at a nursing-facility level, the Administrator reviews continued placement under ADM-04.
The Administrator keeps a list of residents with open HMAs and delegations, with next RN reassessment due dates, and reviews it monthly.

The RN reassesses each HMA on any change of condition, at least annually, and at least every 6 months for a resident with Alzheimer's disease or a related disorder or a resident in a certified facility or unit. Staff notify the RN the same day they notice a change in the resident's condition or the stability of the task.

If the RN finds that the condition is no longer stable and predictable or that the resident no longer directs the task, staff stop performing the HMA at once, and the RN, the physician, the Administrator and the representative decide on next steps. Service plan changes are made under ADM-03.
The Administrator reviews HMA and delegation records, reassessment dates and any HCSSA coordination as part of quality assurance (GOV-04) at least quarterly.

If any task is performed without the required assessment, delegation or training, the Administrator stops it, consults the RN, assesses any harm to the resident, and files the report required by SAF-02 and REC-02 as applicable.

responsibilities.duty: Assigns the RN, makes sure no staff perform tasks beyond personal care without an RN determination, tracks reassessment due dates, and coordinates outside providers.
Assesses and documents whether tasks qualify as HMAs, delegates and supervises under 22 TAC Chapter 225, trains staff, and reassesses on the required schedule.
Perform only tasks they have been trained and cleared to perform, document each performance, and report changes to the RN and Administrator.
Directs the task, gives written agreement, and tells staff when the resident's condition or wishes change.

documentation: RN assessment determining HMA status
Resident or representative written agreement to the HMA
RN delegation records and staff training and competence records
HMA and delegation tracking list with reassessment due dates
Service plan entries for HMAs, delegations and outside providers
Agreements and contact information for HCSSAs and independent health professionals
Records of reassessments and any stopped tasks

policies.title: Change of Condition, Physician Notification and Hospital Transfer
policies.applies_to: All staff, Administrator/Manager, consulting nurse, residents and representatives
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] responds promptly to accidents, injuries, acute illness and significant changes in a resident's condition, notifies the physician and family or responsible party, arranges emergency care or transfer, and updates the service plan.
policies.policy: After an accident or injury that needs emergency medical, dental or nursing care, [AGENCY NAME] arranges emergency care or transfer, immediately notifies the resident's physician and the next of kin, responsible party or placing agency, and documents the event on a separate report that includes a statement of final disposition. Unusual reactions to medications or treatments are reported immediately to the physician and the responsible party. When a resident has a significant change in condition, the service plan is updated, and the Administrator considers whether the resident is now inappropriately placed (see ADM-05). For STAR+PLUS HCBS members, significant changes are reported to the managed care organization (MCO) by the next business day. First aid supplies for burns, cuts and poisoning are kept in one location.

definitions.definition: A noticeable change in a resident's physical, mental or functional status, including acute illness, injury, new or worsening symptoms, an unusual medication reaction, or a decline in ability to perform daily activities.
A change that is not expected to be short-term or that affects the resident's care needs, and that requires an update to the service plan.
The outcome of an event, such as treated on site, sent to the hospital, or returned to the facility, recorded on the report.
The person or agency the resident has designated or who is legally authorized to act for the resident.
The STAR+PLUS managed care organization that contracts with the facility for a Medicaid member's HCBS assisted living services.

procedures: Any staff member who notices a change in a resident's condition, or an accident or injury, stays with the resident, assesses safety, and calls the person in charge. If the situation appears life-threatening, staff call 911 first.

The person in charge provides first aid within the staff member's training, using the supplies in the single first aid location, and decides whether emergency medical, dental or nursing care is needed.

If emergency care is needed, the person in charge arranges it or arranges transfer to a hospital. Staff send with the resident, or provide to emergency personnel, the face sheet, current medication profile, physician and representative contacts, advance directive and any do-not-resuscitate order (RR-06).

The person in charge immediately notifies the resident's physician and the next of kin, responsible party or placing agency, and records the name of the person notified, the date and the time. If no one can be reached, staff keep trying and document each attempt.

If the resident has a possible unusual reaction to a medication or treatment, staff notify the physician and the responsible party immediately and follow the physician's instructions. Staff record the observed signs and the medication involved.

For a change of condition that is not an emergency, staff report it to the Administrator or consulting nurse the same shift. The Administrator or consulting nurse decides whether to notify the physician, and the notification and any orders are documented.

The staff member who witnessed or discovered the event completes a separate incident or accident report before the end of the shift. It describes what happened, the resident's condition, actions taken, who was notified, and the final disposition. The Administrator reviews it by the next business day (SAF-02).
If an injury of unknown origin or other circumstances suggest abuse, neglect or exploitation, the Administrator follows SAF-01 and reports to HHSC as required in REC-02.

When a resident is hospitalized, the Administrator or designee contacts the hospital, shares needed information with the resident's authorization, and tracks the resident's status. Before the resident returns, the Administrator reviews discharge orders and any new medications or treatments with the consulting nurse.

On return, the Administrator or designee compares the discharge orders with the medication profile, gets new orders as needed, reviews the resident's needs, and decides whether the facility can still meet them. The review is documented.

The Administrator, with the consulting nurse, determines whether the change in condition is significant. If it is, the service plan is reassessed and updated within the timeframe in ADM-03, and the resident and representative are informed of the changes.

If the resident's needs now exceed what the facility is licensed or able to provide, the Administrator follows ADM-05, including the inappropriate placement forms due within 10 working days and the evacuation waiver or discharge process as applicable, and ADM-06 for notice requirements.

For a STAR+PLUS HCBS member, the Administrator or designee reports significant changes, such as hospitalization, injury, a decline in health, or a change in ability to be served in the facility, to the member's MCO by the next business day, and records the date, time, person reached and information given.

The consulting nurse and Administrator check the first aid supplies monthly and after use, restocking burn, cut and poisoning supplies and keeping them in one location known to all staff. Staff are told where they are during orientation (STF-03).
The Administrator reviews incident and change-of-condition reports at least monthly for trends and brings concerns to quality assurance (GOV-04).

responsibilities.role: Staff member who finds the change
responsibilities.duty: Stays with the resident, calls for help or 911, provides first aid within training, and reports to the person in charge right away.
Arranges emergency care or transfer, notifies the physician and representative immediately, and ensures the report is completed.
Reviews reports, ensures the service plan is updated, evaluates placement, notifies the MCO by the next business day when applicable, and reports to HHSC as required.
Advises on changes in condition, reviews hospital discharge orders, and helps keep the first aid supplies stocked.

Record of physician and representative notifications with date, time and person reached
Record of unusual medication reactions and notifications
Updated assessment and service plan after a significant change
Hospital transfer information sent and discharge orders received
MCO notification record for STAR+PLUS members
Inappropriate placement forms and evacuation waiver, if applicable
First aid supply check log

policies.title: Dementia and Memory Care
policies.applies_to: Administrator/Manager, all staff including non-direct staff with recurring resident contact, consulting nurse, residents with Alzheimer's disease or a related disorder, and their representatives
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] trains its staff and provides safe, person-centered care for residents with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders, discloses memory care services accurately, and meets the additional standards that apply if the facility or a unit is Alzheimer's certified.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] provides care to residents with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders only when it can meet their needs. All staff are trained under 26 TAC §553.254, and this policy is the all-staff policy on residents with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders required by §553.255. Personal care staff complete 4 hours of training and pass a competency evaluation before providing personal care to these residents, then complete 2 hours of continuing education each year. The Administrator completes 4 hours of training and a competency evaluation and then 2 hours of continuing education each year. Non-direct staff with recurring contact, such as housekeeping, front desk and maintenance, complete training and a competency evaluation on Alzheimer's disease, person-centered care and behaviors. If [AGENCY NAME] markets memory care, it gives each prospective resident the Memory Care Disclosure Statement before admission, and if it is Alzheimer's certified it also gives HHSC Form 3641. Only a Type B facility or unit may be Alzheimer's certified. [AGENCY NAME] [IS / IS NOT] Alzheimer's certified. If it is certified, it also meets the additional staffing, training, admission, disclosure and physical plant standards of Subchapter F.

definitions.definition: Alzheimer's disease or a related dementia that affects a resident's memory, judgment, communication or behavior.
A Type B facility or a unit of a Type B facility that HHSC has certified to serve residents with Alzheimer's disease under Subchapter F. Type A facilities cannot be certified.
A documented check that a staff member can apply the training, for example by demonstration or testing, and not only that the staff member attended.
Staff such as housekeeping, front desk and maintenance who do not provide personal care but have recurring contact with residents.
The disclosure given to prospective residents and their representatives when a facility markets memory care services.

procedures: The Administrator keeps a list of all residents with a diagnosis of or symptoms consistent with Alzheimer's disease or a related disorder, which is updated at admission, at each assessment and when a change of condition is identified.

Before any new personal care staff member provides personal care to a resident with Alzheimer's disease or a related disorder, the Administrator ensures that the staff member has completed the 4-hour training and passed the competency evaluation. Until then, the staff member does not work independently with these residents.
Each personal care staff member completes 2 hours of continuing education on Alzheimer's disease and related disorders each year, and the Administrator tracks due dates on the training log.
The Administrator completes 4 hours of training and a competency evaluation, then 2 hours of continuing education each year.

Non-direct staff with recurring resident contact complete training and a competency evaluation on Alzheimer's disease, person-centered care and behaviors, as part of orientation and no later than the date set by the Administrator in the training plan (STF-03).

The Administrator issues each trained staff member a certificate and keeps a copy in the personnel file for the retention period in STF-06 and REC-01. If a former employee returns after a gap in employment of less than 2 years, prior training may be credited and the certificate is verified and filed.
This policy is given to all staff at orientation. Each staff member signs that he or she has read it, and it is reviewed with the staff at least annually (GOV-03).

During admission screening (ADM-01), the Administrator and consulting nurse decide whether the facility can meet the prospective resident's needs, including wandering and behavioral risks. If the facility cannot meet them, the person is not admitted (ADM-04).

If [AGENCY NAME] markets memory care, the Administrator gives each prospective resident or representative the Memory Care Disclosure Statement before admission and records the date given. If the facility is Alzheimer's certified, it also gives HHSC Form 3641.

The 14-day assessment and service plan address the resident's cognition, communication, behaviors, wandering or elopement risk, safety, routines and preferences. The plan sets person-centered approaches for staff to follow, and staff are told of the plan before they work with the resident (ADM-02, ADM-03).

For residents with identified elopement risk, staff follow SAF-03. Any behavior management follows SAF-04, and restraints are used only as that policy allows. Staff use redirection and non-drug approaches first.
The RN reassesses any HMA for a resident with Alzheimer's disease or a related disorder at least every 6 months, and on any change of condition (HCS-04).

The Administrator ensures that the emergency plan resident list identifies residents with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders so staff and responders know of their needs during an evacuation (SAF-05).

If [AGENCY NAME] is or seeks to be Alzheimer's certified, the Administrator confirms that the facility is Type B, that the certification is requested and renewed through HHSC, that the extra certification fee is paid with the application, and that the Subchapter F staffing, training, admission, disclosure and physical plant standards are in place before residents are served in the certified unit. The Administrator reviews the rule text and updates this policy accordingly (GOV-02, GOV-03).

The Administrator reviews dementia training records, the resident list, disclosure records and incidents involving residents with dementia at least quarterly in quality assurance (GOV-04), and corrects gaps.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures all required training and competency evaluations are completed and tracked, gives disclosures, maintains the resident list, and keeps certification and Subchapter F compliance where applicable.
Complete training and the competency evaluation before providing personal care, follow each resident's person-centered plan, and report behavior or condition changes.
Complete training and a competency evaluation and use person-centered approaches when interacting with residents.
Helps assess needs, advises on care approaches, and reassesses HMAs every 6 months.

Training log with annual continuing education due dates
Signed staff acknowledgment of this policy
Memory Care Disclosure Statement acknowledgment and, if certified, HHSC Form 3641
List of residents with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders
Service plans with person-centered approaches
Alzheimer's certification records, if certified

policies.title: Falls Prevention
policies.applies_to: All direct care staff, Administrator/Manager, consulting nurse, residents and representatives
policies.purpose: To reduce falls and fall-related injuries by assessing fall risk, planning care, training staff, and responding to and documenting each fall.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] assesses each resident's fall risk as part of the comprehensive assessment and service plan, including physical functioning and transfer status. Direct care staff complete 1 hour of competency-based fall prevention training each year as part of the 6 hours of annual direct-care education. Attendants' 16-hour on-the-job training includes safety measures to prevent accidents and injuries, fall prevention, and emergency first aid for a resident who falls. Each fall is documented on a separate report with a statement of final disposition, and the physician and the responsible party are notified.

definitions.definition: An unplanned event in which a resident comes to rest on the floor or another lower surface, whether or not an injury results, including a resident who is found on the floor.
The likelihood that a resident will fall, based on factors such as history of falls, mobility, balance, medications, vision, cognition and the environment.
The amount and type of help a resident needs to move between bed, chair, toilet and other places.
The outcome of the event, such as no injury, treated on site, or sent to the hospital.

procedures: Within 14 days of admission, the Administrator and consulting nurse include fall risk in the comprehensive assessment, including history of falls, physical functioning, transfer status, gait and balance, vision, continence, cognition, medications that may affect balance, and footwear (ADM-02).

The service plan lists the resident's fall risk and specific measures, such as help with transfers or walking, assistive devices, a toileting schedule, night lighting, clear pathways, and footwear. It is updated annually and on any significant change, including a fall (ADM-03).
Staff are told of each resident's fall risk and measures through the service plan before they work with the resident. The Administrator reviews changes with staff at shift change.

The Administrator or designee inspects resident rooms, hallways, bathrooms and common areas weekly and fixes hazards such as clutter, spills, uneven floors, loose rugs, poor lighting and missing grab bars, and logs the repairs (DL-04).

Each attendant completes 16 hours of on-the-job training that includes accident and injury prevention, fall prevention and emergency first aid for a resident who falls. The Administrator signs off on the training (STF-03).

All direct care staff complete 1 hour of competency-based fall prevention training each year as part of the 6 hours of annual education. The Administrator checks competence by demonstration or testing and records it in the training log.

When a resident falls, the staff member stays with the resident, does not move the resident if a serious injury is suspected, and calls the person in charge. The person in charge assesses the resident, provides first aid within staff training, and calls 911 if there is a suspected fracture, head injury, loss of consciousness or other emergency.

The person in charge immediately notifies the physician and the next of kin, responsible party or placing agency when the fall requires emergency medical care, and otherwise notifies the physician and the responsible party in line with HCS-05. Notifications are recorded with the time and the person reached.

The staff member who witnessed or found the resident completes a separate fall report before the end of the shift, including the date, time, location, circumstances, injuries, actions taken, who was notified and the final disposition. The Administrator reviews it by the next business day.

After a fall, staff monitor the resident for delayed signs of injury, such as pain, bruising, swelling, confusion or change in mobility, for a period set by the physician or consulting nurse, and record observations.

Within 7 days of each fall, the Administrator and consulting nurse review the circumstances and update the service plan, adding interventions where needed, and tell the resident, representative and staff of the changes.

If a resident falls repeatedly or his or her needs increase, the Administrator reviews whether the facility can still meet the resident's needs and follows ADM-05 if the resident may be inappropriately placed.
If circumstances suggest abuse, neglect or an injury of unknown origin, the Administrator follows SAF-01 and the reporting required in REC-02.
For STAR+PLUS HCBS members, a fall that is a significant change or that results in hospital care is reported to the MCO by the next business day (HCS-05).
The Administrator reviews fall reports at least quarterly for trends by resident, time, location and cause and records actions in quality assurance (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures fall risk is assessed, staff are trained, environmental hazards are fixed, each fall is reported and reviewed, and trends are analyzed.
Follow each resident's fall prevention measures, respond to falls safely, and complete reports.
Helps assess fall risk, reviews medication effects, and advises on care after falls.
Responds to falls, arranges emergency care, and makes notifications.

Separate fall report with final disposition
Record of physician and responsible party notifications

Training records for fall prevention (on-the-job and annual 1-hour training)
Quarterly fall trend review

policies.title: Skin Integrity and Pressure Injury Prevention
policies.applies_to: All direct care staff, Administrator/Manager, consulting nurse/RN, residents and representatives, outside health care providers
policies.purpose: To prevent skin breakdown and pressure injuries, to detect skin changes early, and to make sure any wound or treatment care beyond personal care is provided only by the people authorized to provide it.
policies.policy: Chapter 553 has no separate skin integrity rule. [AGENCY NAME] adopts this policy under its rules on assessment and service planning, first aid, coordination of care and scope of care. Nutrition, continence and physical functioning are assessed within 14 days of admission and the service plan addresses the resident's skin risks. Direct care staff provide personal care, repositioning support, hygiene, and observation of the skin, and report changes. Wound or treatment care beyond personal care is done only by a licensed professional, a home and community support services agency (HCSSA) or independent professional engaged by the resident, a staff member under RN delegation, or personal care staff performing a health maintenance activity that the RN has assessed and documented. Sudden changes in condition are reported to the physician and the responsible party. [AGENCY NAME] does not provide ongoing care comparable to that of a nursing facility.

definitions.definition: Localized damage to the skin or underlying tissue, usually over a bony area, caused by pressure or pressure with shear.
The condition of a resident's skin, including color, temperature, moisture, intactness and the presence of redness, bruises, tears, blisters or open areas.
Care such as dressing changes, wound cleansing or treatment of an open area, which is beyond ordinary personal care.
A licensed home and community support services agency.

procedures: Within 14 days of admission, the Administrator and consulting nurse assess each resident's skin-related risks, including nutrition and hydration, continence, mobility and positioning, and any existing skin problems, and record findings in the comprehensive assessment (ADM-02).

If the resident arrives with a wound, pressure injury or skin condition requiring treatment, the Administrator refers it to the consulting nurse before admission is finalized to decide whether the facility can meet the resident's needs without ongoing nursing-facility-level services (ADM-01, ADM-04).

The service plan lists skin risks and measures, such as help with changing position, toileting or incontinence care schedule, hygiene, pressure-relieving cushions or devices ordered by the physician, nutrition and fluids, and skin checks. It is updated annually and on any significant change (ADM-03).

During bathing and dressing, staff look at the resident's skin, including areas over bones, heels, hips, tailbone and between skin folds, and note redness, discoloration, blisters, tears, swelling or open areas.

Staff report any new skin change to the person in charge before the end of the shift. The person in charge notifies the Administrator or consulting nurse the same day and records the date, time, location, size and description observed.

The Administrator or consulting nurse decides whether the physician should be notified. The physician and the responsible party are told promptly of any open area, signs of infection, or sudden or significant change, and the notifications are documented (HCS-05).

Staff keep the resident clean and dry, use skin-protecting practices from the service plan, encourage the resident to change position and move as the resident is able, and offer fluids and meals as in DL-01.

Staff do not perform wound treatment, dressing changes, or other care beyond personal care unless they are cleared to do so. Such care may be done only by a licensed professional, an HCSSA or independent professional engaged by the resident, a staff member under RN delegation, or personal care staff performing an HMA that the RN has assessed and documented (HCS-04).

If the resident wants outside services for wound care, the Administrator helps the resident or representative arrange them with an HCSSA or independent professional, shares the service plan, and coordinates the schedule and supplies. Visit notes are kept in the resident's record (HCS-09).

If a resident's skin condition needs ongoing nursing care comparable to that of a nursing facility, the Administrator, consulting nurse, physician and resident or representative decide on next steps. The Administrator follows ADM-05 and ADM-06 if the resident is no longer appropriate for the facility.
Staff use only first aid for minor skin problems, such as minor cuts and scrapes, with supplies from the single first aid location, and document the care and any follow-up (HCS-05).
For STAR+PLUS HCBS members, a significant skin change or hospitalization is reported to the MCO by the next business day.

Each attendant's on-the-job training includes recognizing and reporting skin changes. The Administrator confirms that staff have been trained on this policy at orientation and at least annually (STF-03).
The Administrator reviews skin condition reports and the number of residents with skin concerns at least quarterly in quality assurance (GOV-04) and adjusts staff training and care practices.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures skin risks are assessed and planned, that only authorized persons provide wound or treatment care, that outside providers are coordinated, and that reports are reviewed.
Observe skin during care, carry out preventive measures, and report skin changes the same shift.
Assesses skin-related needs, advises on notification of the physician, and assesses HMAs and delegation for tasks beyond personal care.
Take part in the service plan, tell staff of skin concerns, and arrange outside services if desired.

documentation: Assessment findings on nutrition, continence and physical functioning
Service plan entries for skin care measures
Skin change reports and notifications to the physician and responsible party
RN assessments, HMA agreements and delegation records for any treatment tasks
HCSSA or independent professional agreements and visit notes
First aid care records
MCO notifications for STAR+PLUS members
Quarterly quality assurance review

policies.title: Hospice and Home Health Coordination
policies.applies_to: All residents who receive hospice, home health or other outside health professional services at the facility; Administrator, Manager, attendants, medication staff and any contracted nurse
policies.purpose: To ensure that outside hospice, home health and independent health professional services are coordinated with the facility's own care so the resident receives consistent, safe care and the facility stays within its licensed scope.
policies.policy: A resident may contract with a home and community support services agency (HCSSA) licensed by the State of Texas, or with an independent health professional, to receive services at [AGENCY NAME]. [AGENCY NAME] coordinates with these providers, shares the information they need, and requires them to share their care plans and document their services. [AGENCY NAME] remains responsible for all care provided at the facility. The facility does not provide ongoing nursing-facility-level services. A resident whose needs, even with outside services, exceed what the facility can safely meet is handled under ADM-04, ADM-05 and ADM-06.

definitions.definition: A home and community support services agency licensed by the State of Texas, such as a home health or hospice agency.
An HCSSA, hospice or independent health professional that the resident (or the resident's representative) contracts with to provide services at the facility.
The sharing of the disclosure statement, rate schedule, service plan, care plans and service documentation between the facility and the outside provider.

procedures: The resident or representative tells the Manager when the resident is considering or has chosen hospice, home health or another outside provider. The Manager records the request in the resident record the same day.
The Manager confirms that the HCSSA holds a current Texas license, or that the independent professional is appropriately licensed. The Manager records how this was confirmed and the date.

The Manager gives the outside provider, with the resident's or representative's permission, the facility disclosure statement, the rate schedule and the current Individual Service Plan (ADM-03). The Manager records the date and the person who received them.
The Manager asks the outside provider for its written plan of care before it starts services at the facility. The plan of care is placed in the resident record.

The Manager and the outside provider agree in writing who performs each task, such as personal care, medication administration, wound care or equipment management. The Manager avoids duplicating tasks or leaving tasks with no assigned person. The Manager records the agreement in the service plan.

Within 14 days, or immediately if the resident's condition has significantly changed, the Manager reassesses the resident and updates the Individual Service Plan to include the outside services (ADM-02, ADM-03).

The Manager reviews the plan with the Administrator to confirm the facility can continue to meet the resident's needs and is not being asked to provide ongoing nursing-facility-level services. If it cannot, the Administrator begins the process in ADM-04 through ADM-06.
Each outside provider documents services at the facility on the day the services are provided. The Manager checks weekly that the documentation is present in or accessible from the resident record.
Attendants record the visit of each outside provider on the daily log. Attendants report new orders, observations or changes in the resident's condition to the Manager the same shift.
When the outside provider gives new medication orders, the Manager or designated staff updates the medication record and follows HCS-01 and HCS-02 before any medication is given.
The Manager holds a care conference with the hospice or home health team at least [FREQUENCY] and whenever there is a change of condition (HCS-05). Conference notes are filed in the resident record.

The Manager lists every outside provider serving a resident, with a 24-hour contact number, on the facility emergency contact list. The list is kept current and is used for emergency notifications in SAF-05.
If the facility must evacuate or shelter in place, the Emergency Preparedness Coordinator notifies each resident's outside providers using the contact list and tells them where the resident will be.
In the event of a death while under hospice care, staff follow HCS-10 and call the hospice agency in addition to the physician and family, in the order stated in the resident's hospice plan.

If an outside provider repeatedly fails to provide care plans, documentation or timely services, the Manager reports this to the Administrator. The Administrator contacts the agency in writing and, if the problem continues, informs the resident or representative of the option to change providers.
The Administrator reviews outside provider coordination for each affected resident during quarterly quality assurance review (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures the facility remains responsible for care at the facility, decides whether a resident can continue to be served with outside services, and resolves provider problems.
Verifies provider licensure, shares required documents, obtains care plans, updates the service plan and holds care conferences.
Follow the service plan, record outside provider visits, and report orders and changes to the Manager the same shift.
Keeps outside providers on the emergency contact list and notifies them during emergencies.

documentation: Verification of outside provider licensure
Record that the disclosure statement, rate schedule and service plan were shared
Outside provider plan of care and daily service documentation
Written task-assignment agreement
Updated Individual Service Plan
Care conference notes
Emergency contact list showing outside providers

policies.title: Death of a Resident
policies.applies_to: All staff; Administrator and Manager responsible for notifications, records, medications and resident property
policies.purpose: To ensure that a resident's death is handled with dignity, that emergency care and notifications occur promptly, that any suspected abuse or neglect is reported, and that medications, funds, property and records are handled correctly.
policies.policy: When a resident appears to have died, staff arrange emergency care or transfer as appropriate, immediately notify the resident's physician and next of kin, responsible party or placing agency, and document the event on a report that includes the final disposition. If a death is believed to be due to abuse or neglect, the facility reports it to HHSC and law enforcement. Medications remaining after a death are separated and disposed of by a Texas-licensed pharmacist. Resident funds and property are accounted for from the facility's financial record. Records are kept as required by REC-01.

definitions.definition: A resident found unresponsive, not breathing and without a pulse, or otherwise appearing to have died, before death has been pronounced.
The documented outcome of the event, including who pronounced death or transferred the resident, the time, and where the resident's body was released.
The person or agency identified in the admission records as the resident's legal representative, next of kin or placing agency.

procedures: The staff member who finds a resident who appears to have died stays with the resident and immediately calls the Manager or the person in charge. The staff member checks the resident's advance directive and any hospice orders on file (RR-06, HCS-09).

Unless a valid directive or hospice plan directs otherwise, staff call 911 immediately and begin emergency care as trained until emergency personnel arrive. Staff follow the instructions of emergency responders.

The Manager or person in charge immediately notifies the resident's physician and the next of kin, responsible party or placing agency. If the resident is receiving hospice, the Manager also calls the hospice agency. Each call is recorded with the name, time and response.

If the death may be due to abuse, neglect or exploitation, the Manager or any staff member with cause to believe this immediately reports to HHSC at 1-800-458-9858 and to the municipal police or county sheriff, and follows SAF-01. Staff do not delay a report to complete other steps.
The Manager preserves the scene and the resident's room when abuse or neglect is suspected, and does not discard items until law enforcement or HHSC says it is permitted.
Staff keep other residents informed in a calm and respectful way, and offer support and the opportunity to speak with the Manager.

When the physician, medical examiner or emergency personnel release the resident, the Manager records who took custody of the body, the funeral home or other receiving party, and the date and time. The Manager ensures the resident's body is treated with dignity and privacy.

The Manager completes a written report on the death the same day. The report includes the circumstances, the time of discovery, actions taken, notifications made and the final disposition. The report is filed in the resident record and a copy given to the Administrator.
The Administrator decides whether the death requires additional reports to HHSC or other agencies, and completes them under REC-02 and SAF-02.
The Manager notifies the resident's STAR+PLUS managed care organization or other payer, if applicable, as required by ADM-07.

The Manager separates the resident's remaining medications from the active supply the same day, records each medication on the medication disposal log (HCS-01), and arranges disposal by a Texas-licensed pharmacist. Medications are not given to family or other staff, and not discarded by facility staff.

The Manager and a second staff member inventory the resident's personal property and any funds the facility holds. Both sign the inventory, which is compared with the facility's financial record for that resident.

The Manager releases the property and any remaining funds to the legal representative or other authorized person in line with the admission agreement, RR-04 and RR-05. The recipient signs a receipt, and the Manager gives the recipient a copy.
The Business Office completes the final accounting of charges and any refund due under RR-04 and records it in the resident's financial record.

The Manager completes the resident record, including the admission form, assessments, service plan, physician orders, advance directives, physician exam, professional service documentation and guardianship papers, and files it for retention as required by REC-01.
The Administrator reviews each death during the next quality assurance meeting (GOV-04) to identify any care, safety or reporting issue.

responsibilities.duty: Calls for help, starts emergency care when appropriate, and makes immediate reports if abuse or neglect is suspected.
Makes notifications, completes the death report, arranges medication disposal, inventories property and files the record.
Decides on additional external reports, oversees final accounting, and reviews the event for quality improvement.
Completes the final account of charges, refunds and any funds held for the resident.

documentation: Death report with final disposition
Log of notifications with time and person contacted
Medication disposal record signed by the Texas-licensed pharmacist
Signed property and funds inventory and receipt
Final financial accounting
Report to HHSC and law enforcement if abuse or neglect is suspected
Complete resident record filed under REC-01

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
policies.applies_to: All employees, contractors, volunteers and managers; all residents
policies.purpose: To protect residents from abuse, neglect and exploitation by preventing, detecting and promptly reporting it as required by Texas rules, and to ensure that no one who has engaged in reportable conduct continues to work with residents.
policies.policy: Residents are free from abuse, neglect and exploitation. Anyone who has cause to believe that a resident has been or may be harmed by abuse, neglect or exploitation, or has died from abuse or neglect, must immediately report to HHSC at 1-800-458-9858 and to the municipal police or county sheriff. The facility investigates every report. A written investigation report is sent to the HHSC state office no later than the 5th calendar day after the oral report. [AGENCY NAME] does not retaliate against anyone who files a complaint or gives information in good faith. Every employee signs a statement, as a condition of employment, that they may be criminally liable for failing to report.

definitions.definition: Harm or the threat of harm to a resident, including physical, sexual, emotional or verbal abuse.
Failure to provide the care, supervision or services a resident needs to avoid harm.
Improper use of a resident's money, property or resources, including financial exploitation.
Abuse or neglect causing harm, sexual abuse, financial exploitation of $25 or more, and emotional or verbal abuse causing harm.
Texas Health and Human Services Commission, which licenses and surveys assisted living facilities.

procedures: Before hire, the Administrator checks the Employee Misconduct Registry and the Nurse Aide Registry and completes the criminal history checks required by STF-02. The facility does not hire or keep anyone listed as unemployable or convicted of an offense that bars employment under Health and Safety Code Chapter 250 (including §250.006).
At hire, each employee signs a statement that they may be criminally liable for failure to report abuse, neglect or exploitation. The Administrator places it in the personnel file (STF-06).
Every new employee receives orientation on abuse, neglect and exploitation reporting before they work alone with residents (STF-03). Reporting abuse is a required orientation topic for all staff.

The Administrator posts a sign showing the HHSC hotline number 1-800-458-9858 where residents, staff and visitors can see it, and gives each resident and representative the hotline number at admission. Receipt is documented in the resident record (RR-01, ADM-01).

Staff watch for signs of abuse, neglect and exploitation, including unexplained injuries, changes in behavior, weight loss, poor hygiene, missing money or property, and fear of a particular person. Staff report concerns to the Manager and are not required to prove abuse before reporting.

A staff member who has cause to believe a resident has been or may be harmed, or has died from abuse or neglect, makes an immediate oral report to HHSC at 1-800-458-9858 (or through the HHSC website) and to the municipal police or county sheriff. The staff member does not wait for the Manager's approval.

The staff member informs the Manager or Administrator as soon as possible after the report is made. If the Manager or Administrator is suspected, the staff member reports directly to HHSC and law enforcement.

The report includes the resident's name, age and address, the person responsible for the resident's care, the nature and extent of the condition, the basis for the reporter's knowledge, and any other relevant information. The person making the report records the date, time and name of the person who took the report.

Staff immediately protect the resident from further harm. They obtain medical care if needed and separate the resident from any alleged abuser. An employee under investigation is removed from direct contact with residents until the Administrator determines the resident is safe.
The Administrator notifies the resident's responsible party and physician unless doing so would interfere with the investigation, according to guidance from HHSC or law enforcement.
The Administrator starts an internal investigation immediately. The Administrator interviews witnesses, collects written statements, preserves evidence and reviews the resident's record.

The Administrator sends a written investigation report to the HHSC state office no later than the 5th calendar day after the oral report and keeps a copy in the incident file. The report is also handled under REC-02 and SAF-02.

The Administrator does not discipline, threaten or retaliate against any person who files a complaint or provides information in good faith. Retaliation by any employee results in discipline up to termination under STF-07.

If HHSC finds that an employee has engaged in reportable conduct, the Administrator immediately suspends the employee and does not reinstate the employee until all appeals are exhausted. The Administrator documents the date of suspension and the outcome.
At least every 12 months, the Administrator repeats the Employee Misconduct Registry and Nurse Aide Registry checks for each employee and records the results in the personnel file.
The Administrator reviews every report, investigation and outcome at the quarterly quality assurance meeting (GOV-04) to identify patterns and update prevention practices.

responsibilities.duty: Report suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation immediately to HHSC and law enforcement, and protect the resident.
Directs the investigation, sends the written report by the 5th calendar day, suspends employees found to have engaged in reportable conduct, prevents retaliation and runs annual registry checks.
Ensures staff know the reporting steps, posts the hotline sign and supports the resident after a report.
Residents are encouraged to report concerns to any staff member, the Ombudsman or HHSC without fear of reprisal.

documentation: Signed criminal liability statement in each personnel file
Registry and criminal check results
Record of each oral report with date, time and person contacted
Written investigation report sent to HHSC and the internal investigation file
Resident record entry of hotline number receipt
Orientation training record
Record of any suspension and outcome

policies.title: Incident and Accident Reporting
policies.applies_to: All staff; Manager and Administrator responsible for documentation and reporting
policies.purpose: To ensure that every accident, injury and acute illness receives a timely response, is documented, and is reported to the people and agencies that must be told.
policies.policy: Staff respond immediately to any accident, injury or acute illness involving a resident. Each event is documented on a separate incident report with a statement of final disposition, and the report is kept on file. The physician and the next of kin, responsible party or placing agency are notified immediately. Reportable incidents are self-reported to HHSC. First aid supplies are available in the facility.

definitions.definition: Any accident, injury, acute illness, or unusual event that affects the health or safety of a resident.
The documented result of the event, such as treated at the facility, transferred to a hospital, or returned to routine care.
A disease that Texas law requires to be reported to the city, county or health unit authority.
The HHSC online system used by providers for licensing and for submitting self-reported incidents.

procedures: The staff member who witnesses or discovers the event stays with the resident, calls for help and provides first aid within the limits of their training. If the resident needs emergency care, staff call 911 immediately.
Staff check the resident, secure the area and record vital signs where trained to do so. Staff do not move a resident with a suspected fracture, head or spinal injury unless needed for safety.
The staff member immediately notifies the Manager or person in charge.

The Manager or person in charge immediately notifies the resident's physician and the next of kin, responsible party or placing agency. Each call is recorded with the time, the person reached and the instructions given.
If the resident is transferred to a hospital, the Manager follows HCS-05, sends the resident's face sheet, medication list and advance directive, and documents the transfer.

The staff member who witnessed or discovered the event completes a separate incident report before the end of the shift. The report includes the resident's name, date, time, location, a factual description, the resident's condition, actions taken, notifications made and the final disposition. Reports do not contain opinions or blame.
The Manager reviews the report within one working day, adds any follow-up, and files it in the incident file and, as applicable, the resident record.

The Manager checks the resident for further changes at each shift for at least [PERIOD] after the event and documents observations. If the event shows a significant change in condition, the Manager reassesses the resident and updates the service plan (ADM-02, ADM-03).
If the incident involves possible abuse, neglect or exploitation, a staff member immediately reports it under SAF-01.

The Administrator decides whether the event is reportable and, if so, submits the report to HHSC through TULIP or by calling Complaint and Incident Intake at 800-458-9858, and documents the date, time and confirmation. Reporting requirements are cross-checked against REC-02.
If a resident has or is believed to have a reportable disease, the Manager immediately reports it to the city, county or health unit authority and follows SAF-07 for infection control.
At orientation and in annual training, the Manager tells each employee which conditions and events they must report to the manager, and records attendance (STF-03).
The Manager checks the first aid supplies at least [FREQUENCY] and restocks as needed, recording the date and initials on the checklist.
Events caused by disasters or emergency decisions, such as a decision to shelter in place or evacuate, are also handled and reported under SAF-05.

The Administrator reviews all incident reports monthly for trends, such as falls or medication errors, and presents them at the quarterly quality assurance meeting (GOV-04). Corrective actions are recorded.

responsibilities.duty: Respond, give first aid, notify the Manager and write the incident report before the end of the shift.
Notifies physician and family immediately, reviews reports, arranges follow-up and maintains first aid supplies.
Decides on and submits reports to HHSC and public health authorities, reviews trends and ensures corrective action.

documentation: Incident report with final disposition
Notification log showing physician and family contacts
Self-report confirmation from TULIP or Complaint and Incident Intake
Reportable disease report to local health authority
First aid supply checklist
Monthly incident trend review

policies.title: Elopement and Missing Resident
policies.applies_to: All staff; residents at risk of leaving the facility without notice or supervision, including residents with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders
policies.purpose: To prevent residents from leaving the facility unsafely or unnoticed and to ensure a fast and organized response if a resident is missing.
policies.policy: Chapter 553 does not contain a stand-alone elopement rule. This policy implements the rules on supervision, staffing, emergency preparedness and incident reporting. [AGENCY NAME] provides enough staff to give each resident the supervision and care needed to meet basic needs, keeps an attendant in the facility whenever residents are present, and identifies residents with Alzheimer's or related disorders and those needing special assistance. When a resident is missing, staff begin an immediate search, call 911 as stated in this policy, notify the responsible party and physician, and document the event. Any facility certified for Alzheimer's care also follows the physical plant and staffing standards in Subchapter F.

definitions.definition: A resident leaves the facility or its grounds without the knowledge of staff, or without the supervision the resident needs.
A resident whose location is not known and who cannot be found after a quick check of the usual places.
A resident identified by assessment, history or behavior as likely to wander, leave the facility, or become lost.

procedures: At admission and at each assessment, the Manager screens each resident for elopement risk, including a history of wandering, a diagnosis of Alzheimer's or a related disorder, exit-seeking statements and confusion about place (ADM-01, ADM-02).
The Manager records each resident's risk level and the specific supervision measures in the Individual Service Plan (ADM-03). The Manager shares the plan with each shift.
The Manager keeps a current photograph and physical description of each at-risk resident in a place that every shift can find, with the resident's consent or the representative's consent.
The Manager identifies residents with Alzheimer's or related disorders and those needing special assistance on the resident list used in the emergency plan (SAF-05) and updates it at each change.

Staffing and supervision are scheduled according to STF-01 so that an attendant is in the facility whenever residents are present and at-risk residents are supervised as stated in their service plans.

The Maintenance staff test door alarms, delayed-egress or other exit systems, if any, at least [FREQUENCY] and record the date and result. Exits must not be blocked or locked in a way that conflicts with fire safety (SAF-06). A certified Alzheimer's facility follows the physical plant standards of Subchapter F.
Staff do a headcount at the start of each shift and at [TIMES] during the day, and before and after outings, activities and transportation (DL-03, DL-05). The headcount is recorded.
When a staff member cannot find a resident, the staff member immediately tells the person in charge and does not wait to see if the resident returns.

The person in charge starts the search at once. The person in charge assigns staff to check the resident's room, bathrooms, common areas, outdoor areas, vehicles, and nearby places the resident is known to go, and notes the time the resident was last seen and what the resident was wearing.
The person in charge uses the minimum staffing needed to continue care for other residents and calls additional staff in if needed.

If the resident has not been found after the initial search, no more than [MINUTES] minutes after the alarm, or immediately if the resident is believed to be in danger, the person in charge calls 911, gives the description and photograph, and tells the Administrator.
The person in charge immediately notifies the resident's responsible party and physician. Each call is recorded with the time and the person reached.

When the resident is found, staff check for injury, obtain medical care if needed (HCS-05) and return the resident to a safe setting. The person in charge notifies the responsible party, physician, Administrator and law enforcement that the resident was found.

The person in charge completes an incident report the same shift under SAF-02. If the resident is believed to have been harmed by neglect, the Administrator reports to HHSC at 1-800-458-9858 and to law enforcement under SAF-01 and §553.273.

The Manager reassesses the resident within [PERIOD] after the event, updates the Individual Service Plan with additional protections, and decides whether the facility can continue to meet the resident's needs (ADM-04).

The Administrator reviews each event at the quality assurance meeting (GOV-04) and trains staff on any changes made. At least annually, the Manager runs a missing-resident drill on each shift and records the date, time to complete the search and any problems.

responsibilities.duty: Watch at-risk residents, do headcounts, and immediately report a missing resident.
Directs the search, calls 911 at the set limit, notifies responsible party and physician, and completes the incident report.
Identifies at-risk residents, updates service plans, keeps resident photographs and runs drills.
Ensures staffing and physical safeguards, makes reports to HHSC, and reviews events for corrective action.
Test and maintain door alarms and exit systems and fix defects immediately.

documentation: Elopement risk screening in the assessment and service plan
Resident list with at-risk and special-assistance residents
Headcount records
Door alarm test log
Incident report and notification log
Report to HHSC and law enforcement, if applicable
Missing-resident drill record

policies.title: Restraints and Restrictive Practices
policies.applies_to: All staff, contracted health professionals, residents and representatives
policies.purpose: To protect residents' right to be free from restraint used for discipline or convenience and to ensure that restraint is used only under the conditions Texas rules allow.
policies.policy: Residents are free from physical and chemical restraints used for discipline or convenience. A physical or chemical restraint may be used only with written physician authorization or in an emergency to protect the resident or others from injury. The authorization must specify the circumstances and duration. Except in an emergency, only qualified medical personnel may administer restraints. [AGENCY NAME] uses alternatives and de-escalation first. Residents and representatives are told the facility's restraint and seclusion policy before or at admission.

definitions.definition: Any method or device that restricts a resident's freedom of movement or normal access to the body and that the resident cannot easily remove.
A medication used to control behavior or restrict freedom of movement that is not a standard treatment for the resident's medical condition.
A situation in which a resident's behavior presents an immediate risk of injury to the resident or others and less restrictive measures have not worked.
Use of a restraint to make caregiving easier or to make up for inadequate staffing, rather than to meet a resident's medical need.
Licensed health professionals permitted by Texas law and their license to administer the restraint.

procedures: The Administrator prohibits the use of any physical or chemical restraint for discipline or convenience. Staff who use a restraint for these reasons are subject to discipline up to termination (STF-07) and a report under SAF-01.

Before or at admission, the Manager gives the resident and representative written notice of HHSC rules and the facility's policy on restraint and seclusion, and records the date and the recipient's signature in the resident record (ADM-01).

Staff first use less restrictive approaches, including redirection, a calm environment, meeting unmet needs such as pain, hunger, toileting or boredom, and offering activities (DL-03, HCS-06). The service plan records the approaches that work for each resident (ADM-03).

A physical or chemical restraint is not used unless the resident's physician has issued written authorization, or an emergency exists. The written authorization specifies the circumstances in which the restraint may be used and the duration.

The Manager files the written physician authorization in the resident record and puts a copy where the staff who may use or monitor the restraint can see it. The Manager reviews the authorization before its stated end date and asks the physician to renew or discontinue it.

If a resident has an intellectual disability and a court-appointed guardian, the Manager obtains the guardian's informed consent before any behavior modification involving restraints or adverse stimuli is used, and files the written consent in the record.

In an emergency, staff use only the minimum restraint needed to prevent injury and for the shortest time. Only qualified medical personnel may administer the restraint, except where no one else can act safely in time. Staff call 911 or the physician at once for help.
Staff observe a restrained resident continuously, provide for the resident's comfort, safety, hygiene and breathing, and release the restraint as soon as the emergency ends.

The staff member in charge immediately notifies the Manager, the physician and the resident's representative of any emergency use of restraint. Each notification is recorded with the time and person reached.
