policies.title: Employee and Contractor Vaccination Policy
policies.applies_to: All employees and direct-care contractors of [AGENCY NAME], with requirements set by each person's risk of exposure and of transmitting vaccine-preventable disease to residents.
policies.purpose: To protect residents from vaccine-preventable diseases by maintaining a written policy that meets Texas Health and Safety Code Chapter 224 and 26 TAC §553.261, and by documenting each person's compliance or exemption.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a written policy that requires employees and direct-care contractors to receive the vaccines the facility specifies, based on the person's risk of exposure to and transmission of vaccine-preventable disease. The policy lists the required vaccines, sets verification procedures, and provides exemptions for medical contraindications or precautions identified by the CDC. It states protective measures for exempt employees and prohibits retaliation against medically exempt employees. It requires a written or electronic record of each person's compliance or exemption and states disciplinary action for non-compliance. The facility may also allow exemption for reasons of conscience, including religious beliefs, and may bar exempt staff from resident contact during a public health disaster. Each employee's compliance or exemption record is kept in the personnel file (26 TAC §553.257).

definitions.definition: A disease for which a vaccine is available, such as influenza, hepatitis B, measles, mumps, rubella, varicella, pertussis or COVID-19.
An exemption supported by a written statement from a physician or other authorized provider identifying a CDC-recognized contraindication or precaution to a specified vaccine.
An exemption, if the facility chooses to allow it, based on reasons of conscience including religious beliefs, requested in writing by the employee.
A contractor who provides hands-on care or has recurring direct contact with residents in the facility.
Steps required of an exempt employee to reduce transmission risk, such as wearing a mask during specified periods, hand hygiene, symptom monitoring, or reassignment.

procedures: The Administrator and consulting physician or registered nurse review the vaccines the facility will require and record them in the Vaccine Schedule (Attachment to this policy): [VACCINES SPECIFIED BY FACILITY]. They base requirements on each job category's risk and review the schedule annually and when CDC recommendations change.
At the job offer, HR gives each candidate and direct-care contractor the written Vaccination Policy, the Vaccine Schedule and the exemption request form, and the person signs an acknowledgment.

Before the first day of work, HR collects verification for each required vaccine. Verification can be an immunization record, a provider's statement or titer results as the Vaccine Schedule specifies. HR files it in the personnel file or contractor file.
If the person lacks a required vaccine, HR records the due date. The person receives the vaccine, or submits an exemption request, within the time the Vaccine Schedule specifies.

For a medical exemption, the person submits a written statement from a physician or other authorized provider identifying the CDC-recognized contraindication or precaution. The Infection Prevention Coordinator reviews it for completeness and files it.

If the facility allows exemption for reasons of conscience, including religious beliefs, the person submits a signed request. The Administrator reviews it and responds in writing within 10 calendar days.

For each approved exemption, the Infection Prevention Coordinator identifies and documents protective measures, such as masking, hand hygiene or symptom monitoring, and the employee signs that they understand them.

During a public health disaster, the Administrator may bar employees exempt on conscience grounds from resident contact. The Administrator documents the decision, the period, and any alternative assignment.

Medically exempt employees are never retaliated against: no discipline, reduced hours or loss of pay or benefits is imposed because of the medical exemption. Supervisors who retaliate are subject to discipline. Questions about retaliation go to the Administrator or [CORPORATE COMPLIANCE CONTACT].

HR maintains a written or electronic Vaccine Compliance Record for each employee and contractor showing the vaccines required, the dates received or the exemption type, and the protective measures. A summary is available for HHSC review.

Non-compliance (no vaccine, exemption or documentation by the due date) results in progressive discipline under the Employee Handbook: a written notice, removal from direct resident contact until compliant, and, if non-compliance continues past [NUMBER] days, termination of employment or contract. Each step is documented.
HR notes in the personnel file whether the employee is compliant, exempt or non-compliant, as required by 26 TAC §553.257.

Each year the Infection Prevention Coordinator offers seasonal vaccines such as influenza and reviews each employee's record. HR updates the compliance records and reports to the Administrator the number of compliant, exempt and non-compliant employees.
The QA Committee reviews vaccine compliance rates and any exposure outbreaks at least annually and recommends policy changes.
The Administrator reviews this policy annually and when HHSC or the CDC issues changes, and documents the review in the policy control log (see GOV-03).

responsibilities.duty: Approves the policy and the Vaccine Schedule, decides conscience exemptions and public health disaster restrictions, and enforces discipline.
Advises on required vaccines, risk categories and CDC contraindications.
Reviews exemption documents, sets protective measures, and monitors compliance.
Collects verification, keeps compliance records current, and files them in the personnel file.
Ensure exempt staff follow protective measures and never retaliate against medically exempt employees.

documentation: Written Vaccination Policy and Vaccine Schedule with annual review dates
Signed policy acknowledgments
Immunization verification for each employee and direct-care contractor
Medical exemption statements and (if allowed) conscience exemption requests and decisions
Protective measure acknowledgments for exempt staff
Employee Vaccine Compliance Record in each personnel file
Discipline records for non-compliance

policies.title: Personnel Records
policies.applies_to: All personnel files for employees, including the manager and backup manager, and files for direct-care contractors where noted. Administrator, HR and the Compliance Designee are responsible.
policies.purpose: To keep current and complete personnel records that show each person was screened, trained and qualified before and during employment, and that are available for HHSC review.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps a current, complete personnel record for every employee, available for HHSC review (26 TAC §553.257). Each file holds criminal history check documentation; annual Employee Misconduct Registry (EMR) and Nurse Aide Registry (NAR) results; TB screening; vaccine compliance or exemption; the signed statement on criminal liability for failure to report; and the signed disclosure statement on §250.006 convictions and residence in another state in the past 5 years. Files also hold documentation of orientation, 16-hour on-the-job training, annual education hours and competency (26 TAC §553.253), the manager's 24-hour course evidence with content, hours, dates and provider, Alzheimer's and related disorders training certificates (26 TAC §553.254), the medication aide permit if applicable, and any RN delegation records.

definitions.definition: The employee's file, kept in paper or electronic form, containing required compliance documents and training records.
The HHSC Employee Misconduct Registry, which lists unlicensed persons found to have committed reportable conduct and are barred from employment.
The HHSC Nurse Aide Registry, which lists certified nurse aides and findings of abuse, neglect or misappropriation.
A documented demonstration or test showing the employee can perform a skill or has mastered required training content.
Documentation of a registered nurse's delegation of a task to an unlicensed person, including training, the task and the delegation instructions.

procedures: The Administrator designates HR as custodian of personnel records and keeps a list of personnel file contents in the HR Manual, using a standard file checklist for each employee.
Before the first day of work, HR creates a personnel file using the file checklist and opens a separate, locked confidential medical section.

Before hire, HR searches the EMR and NAR, and prints or saves the results with date and name of the person who searched them. Persons listed as unemployable, or convicted of a barring offense, are not hired.

HR files criminal history check documentation for each employee, including any name-based criminal check in each state of residence in the past 5 years. See STF-02 for hiring restrictions while results are pending.

On or before the first day of work, the employee signs and HR files the statement on criminal liability for failure to report abuse, neglect or exploitation, and the disclosure statement on §250.006 convictions and residence in another state in the past 5 years.
HR files TB screening documentation (see STF-04) and the vaccine compliance or exemption record (see STF-05) in the personnel file by the due dates in those policies.

HR files documentation of orientation (4 hours for all staff), the 16 hours of attendant on-the-job training, and competency evaluations, each with dates, content, hours, trainer name and the employee's signature.

For each year of employment, HR files records of annual direct-care education (including fall prevention and behavior management), and annual geriatric in-service where applicable to nurses, CNAs and medication aides, with dates, hours and topics.

For the manager and backup manager, HR files the written designation, evidence of qualifications (education or experience), and evidence of the 24-hour ALF management course with content, hours, dates and provider, the 8 hours on standards completed within 3 months, and annual continuing education.

HR files Alzheimer's disease and related disorders training certificates and competency evaluations for managers, personal care staff and non-direct staff with recurring contact, as 26 TAC §553.254 requires. HR keeps certificates in the file after employment gaps of under 2 years and re-trains after longer gaps.
HR files a copy of the medication aide permit, with expiration date, and any RN delegation records, including the delegating nurse, task, date and training.
At least every 12 months, HR repeats the EMR and NAR searches, files the dated results and updates the Personnel Compliance Tracker. HR reports any new listing to the Administrator the same day.
HR keeps Form I-9 (8 USC 1324a) in a separate I-9 binder or system, not in the personnel file, and retains it for 3 years after the hire date or 1 year after employment ends, whichever is later.

Each month HR audits at least 10 percent of personnel files, or all files if the facility has fewer than 10 employees, against the checklist. The Administrator reviews missing items and sets correction dates in writing.

The Administrator and HR keep files secure in a locked cabinet or access-controlled electronic system, limit access to those with a business need, and give HHSC surveyors prompt access to files on request.
After employment ends, HR keeps the personnel file for at least [RETENTION PERIOD, set with counsel] and then destroys it by shredding, documenting the destruction.

responsibilities.duty: Owns the personnel record system, reviews audit findings and ensures files are available to HHSC.
Builds, maintains and audits personnel files, repeats EMR and NAR checks, and keeps the compliance tracker.
Provides training records, certificates and competency evaluations to HR.
Provides delegation records and competency sign-offs.
Sign required statements, supply certificates and permits, and report changes in conviction or residence information.

documentation: Personnel file checklist for each employee
Criminal history check documentation and out-of-state checks
Dated EMR and NAR search results at hire and at least every 12 months
Signed statement on criminal liability for failure to report
Signed §250.006 and 5-year residence disclosure statement
TB screening and vaccine compliance or exemption records
Orientation, on-the-job training, annual education and competency records
Manager designation and 24-hour course evidence
Alzheimer's training certificates
Medication aide permit and RN delegation records
Monthly personnel file audit records
Form I-9 (separate file)

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
policies.applies_to: All employees, volunteers and contractors of [AGENCY NAME] who have contact with residents, their families or their property.
policies.purpose: To set clear standards of conduct and professional boundaries so that residents are treated with dignity and are free from abuse, neglect and exploitation, and so staff know their duty to report.
policies.policy: Staff may not abuse, neglect or exploit residents. Financial exploitation of $25 or more is reportable conduct under 26 TAC §553.257, and [AGENCY NAME] prohibits taking or using a resident's money or property in any amount. Staff may not retaliate against any person who files a complaint or gives information (26 TAC §553.273). Every staff member acknowledges in writing their duty to report suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation and their possible criminal liability for failure to report. Residents may refuse to perform services for the facility except as contracted (26 TAC §553.267). Staff respect residents' privacy, dignity and personal property, and maintain professional boundaries at all times.

definitions.definition: The limit that separates a caregiver's professional role from a personal, financial, romantic or social relationship with a resident or the resident's family.
Conduct that HHSC finds, after investigation, includes abuse or neglect causing harm, sexual abuse, financial exploitation of $25 or more, and emotional or verbal abuse causing harm.
The illegal or improper act or process of using a resident or the resident's resources for monetary or personal benefit, profit or gain.
Any adverse action, such as discipline, threats, harassment, schedule changes or discharge, taken against a person because they reported a concern, filed a complaint or gave information.

procedures: At hire, HR gives each employee the Staff Code of Conduct and this policy. Before beginning work the employee signs the acknowledgment and the statement that they may be criminally liable for failure to report abuse, neglect or exploitation. HR files both in the personnel file.

During orientation (4 hours) and annual training, the Staff Development Coordinator covers dignity, independence and choice, resident rights, conflict resolution, professional boundaries and the reporting duty, and records attendance and competency.

Staff provide care in a respectful manner: knock before entering and wait for a reply, address residents by their preferred name, close doors and curtains during personal care, and honor choices about routines, clothing and activities.

Staff never use physical force, threats, intimidation, ridicule, yelling, name-calling or humiliating treatment toward a resident, and never withhold food, care, medication or assistance as punishment or for staff convenience.

Staff never take, borrow, accept or use a resident's money, property, credit cards, checks, ID or bank information, regardless of amount, and never buy or sell items to or from residents. Staff handle resident funds only under RR-05.

Staff do not accept gifts of money, or any gift from a resident or family valued over [NOMINAL GIFT LIMIT], do not accept tips, and do not accept appointments as agent, power of attorney, executor or beneficiary of a resident. Staff report any offer of such gifts to the Administrator the same day.

Staff do not have romantic or sexual relationships with residents, share personal social media with residents or families, or use resident photos or information on social media or messaging apps. Staff report any such contact to the Administrator.

Staff do not ask residents to perform services for the facility, such as cleaning, laundry, kitchen work or errands, except where the admission agreement provides for the service. A resident may decline without consequence, and the Administrator reviews any exception.
Staff respect resident privacy and confidentiality (see RR-07), and do not discuss residents outside the work setting or in front of other residents or visitors.

Staff who see or suspect abuse, neglect or exploitation make an immediate oral report to HHSC at 1-800-458-9858 and to local law enforcement, and notify the Administrator, following SAF-01. The Administrator may not delay or screen the report.

The facility does not retaliate against any person who files a complaint or gives information. Supervisors do not alter schedules, assignments or pay because of a report. Any employee who retaliates is disciplined, up to and including termination.

When an allegation involves a staff member, the Administrator removes the employee from resident contact pending the outcome of the investigation, documents the action and notifies HHSC as required under SAF-01 and REC-02.

If HHSC finds an employee engaged in reportable conduct, the Administrator suspends the employee and does not reinstate the person until all appeals are exhausted, as required by 26 TAC §553.257. HR checks the EMR and NAR and files the results.

The Administrator investigates violations of this policy, interviews witnesses, documents findings, and takes disciplinary action under the Employee Handbook, ranging from corrective action to termination, in all cases within [NUMBER] business days of the report.
The Administrator reviews conduct complaints and findings quarterly with the QA Committee and updates training topics as needed.

responsibilities.duty: Enforces the Code of Conduct, removes accused staff from resident contact, investigates, disciplines and prevents retaliation.
Model respectful care, observe staff-resident interactions and report concerns immediately.
Provides training on dignity, resident rights, boundaries and conflict resolution.
Obtains and files signed acknowledgments and conducts registry checks.
Follow the Code of Conduct and report suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation immediately.

documentation: Signed Staff Code of Conduct acknowledgment
Signed statement on criminal liability for failure to report
Training attendance and competency records on dignity, resident rights, boundaries and conflict resolution
Incident and investigation records
Disciplinary records
Records of gift offers reported to the Administrator
EMR and NAR results following any HHSC finding

policies.title: Resident Records and Retention
policies.applies_to: All clinical, administrative and financial records for current and former residents of [AGENCY NAME], in paper or electronic form.
policies.purpose: To keep complete, confidential and accessible resident records that meet 26 TAC §553.265 and support quality care, resident rights and HHSC review.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps a record for every resident that contains the standard admission form, assessments, the service plan, physician orders, advance directives, the physician exam (within 30 days before or 14 days after admission, unless the resident is exempt, such as a Christian Scientist), documentation of services by health professionals, and guardianship papers (26 TAC §553.265). Records are confidential and safeguarded and are available to residents, their legal representatives and HHSC. The facility keeps a simple financial record of charges and of any personal funds it holds, and issues receipts on request. The retrieved §553.265 sets no fixed retention period for resident records. As facility policy, [AGENCY NAME] keeps resident records for at least 6 years after discharge or death, in line with the HIPAA documentation period, and longer if counsel advises or a legal hold applies.

definitions.definition: The set of documents, in any format, that describes a resident's admission, assessments, services, health care, finances and legal status.
A guardian, agent under a medical or financial power of attorney, or other person authorized by law to act for a resident.
The court order appointing a guardian and the letters of guardianship showing current authority.
A directive to preserve records because of pending or anticipated litigation, investigation or a request from a regulator.

procedures: The Administrator designates a Records Custodian, and the custodian keeps a standard record index (tabs or electronic folders) for each resident record in the Records Manual.

At admission, the admission coordinator opens the record and files the signed admission agreement and the standard admission form, the pre-admission screening and the disclosure statement acknowledgment.

The coordinator obtains the physician exam done within 30 days before or 14 days after admission, along with physician orders, and files them. If the resident is exempt from the exam, the coordinator documents the exemption basis.
The RN or assessor files the comprehensive assessment and the service plan within 14 days of admission, and files later reassessments and plan updates as they occur (see ADM-02 and ADM-03).
Staff file advance directives, resident choices and copies of any medical or financial power of attorney the resident provides (see RR-06).

Staff file documentation of services by health professionals and outside providers, such as physician visits, therapy, home health and hospice notes, in the record within [NUMBER] business days of receipt.

Staff file the medication profile and missed-dose records, monthly self-administration counseling records where applicable, authorized electronic monitoring forms, and incident reports, in the clinical record.

At admission and at each annual assessment, the Records Custodian asks in writing for the guardianship court order and letters if the resident has a guardian. The same request is made when the facility learns that a guardian has been appointed. The custodian makes at least one follow-up request within 30 days, and files the results, copies and request dates.
The business office maintains a simple financial record of charges and of any personal funds held for the resident, and gives a receipt on request (see RR-05).
The Dietary Manager keeps menus as served for 30 days, and posts them as required in DL-01.

Residents and their legal representatives may review their records on request. Staff schedule review within [NUMBER] business days, supervise review, document it, and provide copies as the law and facility copy-fee policy allow.
The Administrator gives HHSC surveyors immediate access to records on request and documents the records reviewed.

Records are confidential: staff access records only for assigned duties, keep paper records in locked areas and use unique logins and password protections for electronic records, in line with RR-07. Staff do not leave records unattended or copy them outside the facility.
When a resident is discharged or dies, the Records Custodian completes the record within 30 days, marks the discharge or death date and stores it securely.

The Records Custodian keeps resident records for at least 6 years after discharge or death, and longer if counsel advises or a legal hold applies. The custodian places a hold on any record involved in a pending complaint, investigation or lawsuit.

At the end of the retention period, the custodian approves destruction in writing with the Administrator, shreds paper records, permanently deletes electronic records, and keeps a destruction log of the resident name, dates and method. If the facility closes or changes ownership, the Administrator arranges secure transfer or storage of records and notifies HHSC as required.
The Administrator audits a sample of open and closed records quarterly for completeness and reports findings to the QA Committee.

policies.title: Required Reports and Notifications to HHSC and Others
policies.applies_to: The Administrator, manager, Emergency Preparedness Coordinator, Infection Prevention Coordinator, nursing and business office staff, and any employee responsible for making or supporting a required report.
policies.purpose: To make sure that every report and notification required of an assisted living facility is made to HHSC, law enforcement, the local health authority, the Emergency Management Coordinator or the managed care organization (MCO), on time, with the right content, and is documented.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] makes all required reports and notifications on time and keeps proof of each. Suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation is reported orally and immediately to HHSC (1-800-458-9858) and to law enforcement, and a written investigation report goes to the HHSC state office no later than the 5th calendar day after the oral report (26 TAC §553.273). HHSC is notified before the immediate termination of a resident who is a serious threat (26 TAC §553.267). Inappropriate placement forms (1124, 1125, 1126) or the evacuation waiver packet go to the HHSC regional office within 10 working days (26 TAC §553.259). The HHSC regional office and the local Emergency Management Coordinator (EMC) are notified immediately of a decision to shelter in place or evacuate (26 TAC §553.275). Reportable diseases among residents are reported immediately to the local health authority (26 TAC §553.261). License renewal is filed at least 45 days before expiration and HHSC approval is obtained before adding beds (26 TAC §553.47). For STAR+PLUS residents, significant changes are reported to the MCO by the next business day. Incidents are reported through TULIP or the 1-800-458-9858 intake line.

definitions.definition: A verbal report made by phone to HHSC intake at 1-800-458-9858 (or through the HHSC website when authorized) and to law enforcement. It is made immediately when staff have cause to believe abuse, neglect or exploitation occurred.
Monday through Friday, excluding state and federal holidays, for purposes of the 10-working-day placement form deadline.
The local Emergency Management Coordinator, who works with the facility on emergency planning and response.
The STAR+PLUS managed care organization that contracts with the facility and coordinates a member's services.
The HHSC online system used for facility applications and provider self-reported incidents.

procedures: The Administrator maintains a Required Reports Matrix listing each report type, trigger, deadline, recipient, responsible person and documentation. The Matrix is posted in the Administrator's office and reviewed at least annually and whenever rules change (see GOV-03).

Abuse, neglect or exploitation: any staff member who has cause to believe a resident has been or may be harmed, or died from abuse or neglect, calls HHSC at 1-800-458-9858 and municipal police or the county sheriff immediately, and notifies the Administrator. The oral report includes the resident's name, age and address, the person responsible, the nature of the condition, the basis of knowledge and other relevant information.

The Administrator investigates the allegation, protects residents, and sends the written investigation report to the HHSC state office no later than the 5th calendar day after the oral report. The Administrator documents the date and time of each report, the person who made it, and any confirmation or intake number. Details are in SAF-01.

Immediate termination of a resident who is a serious threat: before the facility terminates the residency immediately, the Administrator notifies HHSC at 1-800-458-9858 and documents the call, the reason and the safety measures taken. Terminations on 30 days' written notice follow ADM-06.

Inappropriate placement: when assessment shows a resident is inappropriately placed and will be retained, the RN or Administrator completes Forms 1124, 1125 and 1126 or the evacuation waiver packet, and sends them to the HHSC regional office at [REGIONAL OFFICE ADDRESS/FAX] within 10 working days. The Administrator calendars the deadline and keeps proof of sending. If the facility will not retain the resident, discharge is completed within 30 days (see ADM-05 and ADM-06).

Emergency decisions: immediately after deciding to shelter in place or evacuate, the Emergency Preparedness Coordinator (or alternate) notifies the HHSC regional office at [REGIONAL OFFICE PHONE] and the local EMC at [EMC PHONE], logs the time and the person contacted, and follows SAF-05.

Reportable disease: the Infection Prevention Coordinator or RN reports a resident's reportable disease immediately to the local health authority at [LOCAL HEALTH DEPARTMENT PHONE], records the disease, time, person spoken to and any instructions, and follows SAF-07.

License renewal: the Administrator calendars the license expiration date and files the renewal at least 45 days before expiration to avoid the late-renewal fee, which is half of the basic fee (26 TAC §553.47). The Administrator keeps the application confirmation and the license in the regulatory file (see GOV-02).
Adding beds: before admitting residents to any added beds, the Administrator obtains HHSC approval of the capacity increase and pays the per-bed fee, and keeps the approval in the regulatory file.

STAR+PLUS residents: when a STAR+PLUS member has a significant change, such as hospitalization, change of condition, move, death or discharge, the RN or Administrator reports it to the MCO service coordinator by the next business day, and records the name of the person informed and the date and time (see ADM-07).
Other incidents: the Administrator reports incidents through TULIP or the 1-800-458-9858 intake line, in accord with SAF-02, and keeps the confirmation.

For every report, the person making it completes an entry in the Required Reports Log showing the date and time of the triggering event, date and time of the report, recipient, method, content summary and any follow-up needed.

The Administrator checks the log each business day for open items and deadlines, and on weekends the Administrator on call does so. Late reports are reported at once to the Administrator, who makes them immediately and records the reason for the delay.
Quarterly, the QA Committee reviews the Required Reports Log for timeliness and completeness, identifies trends, and updates procedures or training as needed (see GOV-04).
All staff are trained at orientation and annually on which events must be reported, whom to call and the 24-hour phone numbers posted at each nurse or staff station.
